sections.heading: The eight MYP subject groups and the criteria behind each grade
paragraphs: Eight groups, and knowing their names changes how you read a report. Language and Literature. Language Acquisition. Individuals and Societies. Sciences. Mathematics. Arts. Physical and Health Education. Design. Every group is assessed against four criteria labelled A to D, and those criteria mean different things in different groups, which is the single most misunderstood feature of the programme among parents in Mumbai.

Here is where that matters. In Mathematics the four criteria run roughly as knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In Sciences they run as knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In Language and Literature they are closer to analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. In Individuals and Societies the fourth criterion is thinking critically. A student can therefore score at the top of criterion A in every subject and still bring home mediocre grades, because the thing being scored low is investigation, evaluation or communication, none of which is content knowledge. An MYP subject groups tutor in Bhayandar should be able to explain your child's own report in those terms within one session.

The criteria are combined into a subject grade using published boundaries that differ by subject and are revised from time to time, so ask your school's MYP coordinator how your child's grade was arrived at rather than inferring it. What you can rely on is the pattern: a persistent low score on one criterion across several subjects is a skill gap, not a subject problem, and it is the most efficient thing a tutor can fix. A student weak at criterion D in both Sciences and Individuals and Societies is being asked to evaluate and has never been taught how.

That is also why we ask for the report rather than a description of it. An IB MYP tutor in Bhayandar reading actual criteria scores can plan a first month in ten minutes. The same tutor working from "she is struggling in science" will spend three sessions discovering that the science is fine and the write-ups are the problem.

sections.heading: Report cards, criteria and the Mumbai MYP calendar
paragraphs: MYP reporting is the reason most families here start searching, and it arrives on a predictable cycle. Schools report against criteria rather than percentages, usually twice or three times across the year, with an interim comment in between. The first substantial report of the year is the one that produces enquiries, because it is the first time parents see a number attached to a skill they did not know was being assessed. Children in Bhayandar mostly travel south to schools on the Dahisar and Borivali side, among them Singapore International School and JBCN International School, Borivali. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Singapore International School, JBCN International School, Borivali or any other school named here.

The year has its own shape. The first term is the right time to fix a skill gap, because the criteria will be assessed again and there is room for the second score to be better. The months after the December break are when Year 5 personal projects consume evenings and when subject teachers start talking openly about Diploma Programme choices. The final term brings the assessments that set the year's record and, for Year 5, the handover conversations about subject selection. Booking a tutor in the first term is cheaper in every sense than booking one in the last.

The bus run decides the week. A Bhayandar child bussed to Borivali or Dahisar East leaves early and returns late, and for a Year 6 or Year 7 student that means the genuinely teachable window is narrow and ends earlier than parents expect. A tired MYP lesson is worse than no lesson, because it produces evidence the tutor will misread. We would rather book IB home tuition in Bhayandar at the hour your child can actually concentrate, even if that means a weekend morning, than fill a slot that technically exists.

Read report comments as instructions. "Needs to develop evaluation" means criterion D work. "Presents work inconsistently" means communication, which is a criterion and not a personality trait. "Does not transfer skills to new contexts" means application. "Reluctant to contribute" is pastoral rather than academic and a tutor should say so rather than bill for it. Bring the actual report to the discovery call and let the tutor read the criteria scores for themselves.

sections.heading: Why MYP home tuition in Bhayandar beats online for younger years
paragraphs: Because attention is the limiting factor, not expertise. A Year 2 or Year 3 MYP child in a room with an adult will start a task. The same child in front of a screen will start a task, then open another tab, and the tutor will be the last person to notice. For the lower middle years we recommend home tuition first and argue for it even when a family would prefer the convenience of a video call, which is the opposite of the advice we give for a second-year Diploma Programme candidate in the same building.

Bhayandar's distance from the city's International Baccalaureate school cluster pushes most of our Diploma Programme enquiries online, and for the Middle Years Programme it has a different effect: it shortens the list of nearby tutors rather than changing the recommendation. So the honest sequence here is to match an IB MYP tutor in Bhayandar locally for Years 1 to 3 even where that means a strong generalist rather than a subject specialist, and to treat online as the solution for scarce needs only, such as a particular language acquisition or a Design brief nobody local can supervise.

From Year 4 the calculation changes. An older MYP student who can work alone for forty minutes can be taught well online, and by Year 5 an IB online tutor in Bhayandar is often the right answer for a specialist subject, especially where the aim is Diploma Programme preparation. Online works on the same conditions as always: the student writes rather than watches, there is a camera on their own page for mathematics and Design sketches, and somebody has tested the connection at the actual lesson hour rather than at noon.

Hybrid suits Year 4 and Year 5 particularly well. One session at home each week for supervised work and the personal project process, one online for subject drilling with a specialist. It also keeps the cost sensible, since travel time is built into any rate, and a home tutor for MYP subject groups Mumbai families want for a scarce subject becomes affordable when only one weekly session carries the journey north.

sections.heading: Who is allowed to teach your Year 8 child in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Only somebody who has cleared four checks, and for younger children we treat them as non-negotiable rather than reassuring. Government photo identity matched to the profile name. The qualification produced as a document, not described on a call. A subject interview with someone who has taught the programme. References from previous teaching or tutoring, contacted rather than collected. None of that has happened for an IB private tutor Bhayandar families engage through a building notice board, which does not make that person unsuitable, but it does mean the checking is now entirely your responsibility.

The Middle Years Programme interview asks something the Diploma Programme interview does not. We hand over a real criteria-based report card with scores across A to D and ask the candidate to explain to a parent what it says and what they would work on first. Someone who talks only about content has missed the programme. We also ask how they would teach a Year 7 student to evaluate a source, because that is criterion work and it is the commonest unmet need we see. Any IB tutor Mumbai parents are offered through us has answered both of those questions in front of a person who knows the programme.

Then there are the checks only you can run, and the discovery call is where to run them. Ask which MYP years they have taught, specifically, and listen for whether they distinguish between Year 2 and Year 5. Ask what they would do in the first four sessions with your child's report in front of them. Ask what you will receive after each lesson. Ask how they handle a child who says nothing when confused. And be wary of anyone who offers a guaranteed grade: no honest MYP teacher would, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades either.

For home sessions with a younger child, a few practical norms do more than any certificate. An adult in the flat throughout. The lesson at a table in a shared room rather than a bedroom. The door open. Notes after every session. If any of those slip, tell us and it is logged against the profile. Families in Mira Road, Vasai and Dahisar see the same panel as Bhayandar, so one report protects the next household.

sections.heading: The personal project in Year 5, and the jump to the Diploma Programme
paragraphs: The personal project is assessed on process, not on the object produced, and almost every family gets that backwards. A beautifully finished product with no documented planning, no evidence of applied skills and a thin reflection scores poorly. A modest product with a clear goal, honest records of what went wrong and a reflection that names what the student learned about their own working scores well. The process journal is the assessment, and the single most useful thing a tutor does is make the student keep it from the first week rather than reconstruct it in the last.

A case from this corridor, changed in detail. A Year 5 student in Bhayandar, travelling to Borivali daily, chose to build a community recycling guide. By the time her family called, the guide was almost finished and the journal held four entries, all written in one evening. Her tutor stopped work on the product entirely for two sessions and rebuilt the record: what the goal actually was, which skills had been applied and where the evidence sat, what had failed and what she did instead. The product barely changed. The assessment position changed a great deal, because the criteria were finally being addressed.

The transition to the Diploma Programme is the other Year 5 worry, and it is a real one rather than parental anxiety. Three things shift at once. Criteria marking gives way to mark schemes that want precise command word responses. The quantitative load in Sciences and Mathematics increases sharply and assumes fluency the MYP never required under time pressure. And internal assessments arrive with external deadlines rather than classroom ones. A student with strong MYP criteria scores can meet all three and conclude they have become worse at school, when what has changed is the measurement.

So the most useful Year 5 tutoring is not revision. It is building habits the Diploma Programme will demand: timed writing, command word discipline, algebra practised until it is automatic, and the discipline of working from a published assessment description rather than from a teacher's instruction. A term of that in Year 5 is worth considerably more than the same term spent in the autumn of DP1, and it is the one piece of advance work families almost never think to buy. Confirm every project deadline and subject choice date with your school's MYP coordinator rather than any date read online, including on this page.

sections.heading: What should change in a month of MYP tuition in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Behaviour and output, not a criterion score. In four weeks of home tuition in Bhayandar, Mumbai, look for a child who starts written work without negotiation, who can say out loud what a question is asking before answering it, and whose work is laid out so a stranger could follow it. Look also at the tutor's notes: they should name criteria and skills rather than reporting that your son was cooperative. Criterion scores move on the school's assessment cycle, which may be months away, so judging a month of work by a report card is judging the wrong thing.

Across a term the evidence becomes clearer. The criterion that was consistently low starts producing middling scores rather than poor ones, which in criteria marking is a genuine shift. Written work gains structure: a source evaluation that names origin, purpose, value and limitation; a science write-up that processes data before concluding; a mathematics solution somebody else can read. Teachers begin writing different comments, which is often the first external confirmation a family gets. An IB MYP tutor in Bhayandar should be predicting that change and telling you what to look for before it appears.

Across a full year the defensible claim is narrow. A student who works consistently with a well-matched tutor usually improves, and how much depends on where they started, which skills were never taught and how much is practised without the tutor present. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, publishes no success rates and does not allow tutors to promise outcomes. In the Middle Years Programme that caution matters doubly, because criteria scores are awarded by the school on its own judgement and no outside tutor controls them.

The honest limits are worth stating. A tutor cannot change a criterion score directly, cannot sit the assessments, and cannot supply motivation that has to come from a twelve year old. What a tutor can do is teach the skill the criterion is testing, which is the only route to a better score that does not involve wishing. If progress stalls because nothing happens between sessions, we will say so at the review, and sometimes the right advice is a shorter session twice a week rather than more hours.

sections.heading: Starting MYP home classes in Bhayandar
paragraphs: Send four things and the first session earns its fee: the MYP year confirmed by the school, the latest report with the criteria scores visible, one piece of marked work with the teacher's comments on it, and the two after-school windows that are real rather than aspirational. A photograph of the report is worth more than any description, because a tutor reads the pattern across subjects that a parent reading one subject at a time cannot see.

The first session should look like an assessment of skills rather than a lesson in content. Expect a short written task connected to the weak criterion, done without help while the tutor watches what happens. Expect your child to be asked to explain what the question wants. Expect one thing taught properly at the end so she leaves with a win. Then a written note to you naming the skill gap, the order of work for the next four sessions, and what has been set before the next lesson.

Set up the space before the home tutor arrives, and for younger children keep it simple. A table in a shared room, not a bedroom. The school's own exercise books and the marked work, since the tutor needs to see what was actually taught and how it was marked. Pencil case, ruler and a sharpened pencil. No screens in reach unless the lesson needs one. An adult in the flat throughout. Keep the same hour on the same day each week, because for middle years students the rhythm does more work than the content.

On cost, we print no price list, and treat any tutor who quotes one before asking your child's year with scepticism. IB tuition fees in Bhayandar depend on the year and subject group, how scarce the specialism is, travel distance, session length and whether the lesson runs at home or online. A Year 5 Design specialism costs differently from a Year 2 literacy slot. Ask for the per-session rate in writing before the first paid lesson, and ask what happens when you cancel on the day.

faqs.question: What does an IB MYP tutor in Bhayandar actually cost?
faqs.answer: There is no single rate and anyone quoting one before asking your child's year is guessing. IB tuition fees in Bhayandar depend on the MYP year and subject group, how scarce the specialism is, how far the tutor travels, the session length and whether the lesson is at home or online. faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to Bhayandar in time for a 5.30 lesson after the school bus?
faqs.answer: Only from inside the corridor, and that is why we keep the MYP pool tight. Tutors living in Bhayandar, Mira Road, Dahisar or the Borivali edge can hold an early evening slot through a term. Anyone coming from Andheri or further south cannot, because Metro Lines 2A & 7 stop at Dahisar and the last stretch north is road or Western Line at exactly the wrong hour. Tell us the earliest the bus realistically arrives and the latest your child can still concentrate, and we will match inside that window rather than promising outside it.

faqs.question: My daughter gets 7s on criterion A and 3s on criterion D. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: She knows the content and has not been taught the skill the fourth criterion tests, which differs by subject group. In Individuals and Societies criterion D is thinking critically. In Sciences it concerns reflecting on the impacts of science. In Mathematics it concerns applying mathematics in real-life contexts. None of those is knowledge, so revising harder will not move them. The fix is explicit skill teaching with a template she applies repeatedly: for source evaluation, naming origin, purpose, value and limitation every single time until it becomes automatic. This usually shows in work within a month.

faqs.question: How is an MYP grade actually calculated?
faqs.answer: Four criterion scores are combined using published boundaries, and those boundaries differ between subjects and are revised periodically, so ask your school's MYP coordinator how your child's specific grade was arrived at rather than trusting a conversion table found online. What is reliably useful is the pattern rather than the arithmetic. A criterion that is persistently low across several subject groups is a transferable skill gap and the most efficient thing to fix. A single low criterion in one subject is usually a content or teaching issue in that subject alone.

faqs.question: Does the tutor help with the Year 5 personal project?
faqs.answer: Yes, as process coaching rather than production. The personal project is assessed on the process: the goal, the planning, the skills applied and the honest reflection, all evidenced in the journal. A tutor's most valuable intervention is early, insisting the journal is kept weekly from the start, because it cannot be convincingly reconstructed at the end. A tutor can also push a student to narrow an over-ambitious goal and to write reflection that names what failed. A tutor who offers to produce any part of the project is a risk to your child's standing, not a shortcut.

faqs.question: How worried should I be about the jump from MYP to the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Worried enough to act in Year 5, not worried that your child has a problem. Three things change at once: criteria marking gives way to mark schemes wanting precise command word answers, the quantitative load in Sciences and Mathematics rises sharply under time pressure, and internal assessments arrive with external deadlines. A student with strong MYP scores can meet all three and conclude they have got worse, when only the measurement has changed. A term of timed writing, command word work and automatic algebra in Year 5 is worth more than the same term spent repairing DP1.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring suitable for a Year 7 student?
faqs.answer: Usually not as the main arrangement, and we will say so even when it is more convenient. Attention is the limiting factor in the lower and middle MYP years, and a younger student in front of a screen will open another tab while the tutor is the last to know. For Years 1 to 3 we match locally first and accept a strong generalist over a distant specialist. From Year 4 online starts working properly, provided the student writes rather than watches and there is a camera on their own page. By Year 5 it is often the right answer for a scarce subject.

faqs.question: Which MYP subjects do you cover?
faqs.answer: All eight groups: Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design. Availability varies by year band and by how scarce the specialism is, and the honest position is that mathematics, sciences and English arrive quickly while a specific language acquisition or an Arts and Design brief can take longer and may be matched online. Tell us the subject group rather than the teacher's subject name, since schools label courses differently and the group is what determines which criteria apply.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not right for my child?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we replace them, usually inside a week, with no notice period and no minimum number of sessions. The reason matters because it shapes the next match: talks too fast, impatient with repeated questions, treats a twelve year old like a Diploma Programme candidate, sets no work between lessons. Younger students rarely complain directly, so watch for a child who starts finding reasons to miss the slot. We review every two to four weeks for that reason. Sometimes a change of method with the same tutor is quicker and quite sufficient.

faqs.question: Do you cover Mira Road, Vasai and Dahisar for MYP students?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for the middle years those four areas effectively share one tutor pool. Bhayandar and Mira Road slots are commonly paired in the same evening, which is often what makes an early weekday booking viable for the tutor. Vasai households are matched from the Vasai and Nalasopara side wherever the panel allows, because crossing the creek twice in an evening rarely survives a term. Dahisar matters because the metro terminates there, letting a specialist from further south in Mumbai reach the corridor without using the highway at its worst hour.

faqs.question: Should a parent stay at home during a middle years lesson?
faqs.answer: Yes, an adult should be in the flat throughout any home tuition session in Bhayandar, and for younger children we treat it as a firm norm rather than a preference. You do not need to sit in the room. What helps most is a short handover at the end: what was covered, what has been set, what to watch for in the week. Keep the lesson at a table in a shared room with the door open rather than in a bedroom, and keep screens out of reach unless the work needs one. If nobody can be home midweek, use a weekend morning instead.

faqs.question: My son is in Year 4 on the Standard mathematics pathway but wants Higher Level maths later. What now?
faqs.answer: Start the groundwork now rather than in the holiday before the Diploma Programme. The Standard and Extended pathways through the later MYP years differ in algebraic depth, and a student aiming at Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level needs fluency the Standard route may not build. Ask the school what the pathway difference actually covers, then have a tutor work through that delta across Year 4 rather than compressing it later. Also ask the school whether and when a pathway change is possible, since that window is set by them and not by you.

sections.heading: MYP Years 1 to 5: what changes at each stage
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme runs across five years and the demands shift considerably from one end to the other. In the early years the work is about building habits: reading closely, recording work properly, following a method, explaining thinking in writing rather than only out loud. By Years 4 and 5 the tasks look much closer to senior school: extended written responses, independent investigations, sustained projects, and assessment criteria applied with far less scaffolding than before.

That shift is where most families first notice a problem. A child who coasted through Year 2 on quick comprehension can struggle in Year 4 when the task requires planning, structuring and justifying. Nothing has gone wrong with the child; the task has changed category. A tutor who understands this will work on process rather than content, teaching how to plan an answer before writing it, which is the actual deficit. One who does not will revise topics the student already knows and both parties will be puzzled by the lack of progress.

Year 5 adds the personal project and, in many schools, the question of what comes next. Some students continue into the Diploma Programme, which is covered by its own pages here. What belongs on this page is the MYP side of that step: the independent working habits, the written structure and the self-management that the Diploma assumes a student already has. Families who use Year 5 to build those get an easier first Diploma term than families who treat Year 5 as a quiet year before the serious one.

sections.heading: The eight MYP subject groups and where Mumbai students lose bands
paragraphs: The programme covers eight subject groups: Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design. Each is assessed against four criteria, and the criteria differ by subject even where the letters are the same. Criterion B in Mathematics is investigating patterns. Criterion B in Sciences is inquiring and designing. A parent who learns only the letters will mix them up, and so will a tutor who has not taught the group. MYP subject groups tuition in Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) therefore starts from the subject's own criteria rather than from a generic rubric.

The band losses are consistent across cohorts. In Mathematics students find a pattern, describe it, and never generalise it into a rule or justify why it holds, which is where the upper bands live. In Sciences they write a method with no controlled variable or no sensible range, then a conclusion that does not reference their own results. In Language and Literature they retell the text instead of analysing how the writer achieves an effect. In Individuals and Societies they describe sources without evaluating their origin and purpose. In Design the investigation and evaluation stages get compressed because the making was the fun part.

None of those are knowledge failures, which is the single most useful thing a parent can understand about MYP marking. They are failures to do the specific intellectual move the criterion rewards. That is why a strong student can receive a mediocre band and the family concludes the teacher dislikes them. A tutor running MYP subject groups home classes in Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) should be able to read a task, name the move that was missing, and teach it as a repeatable step rather than as a matter of effort.

paragraphs: Children here attend Dhirubhai Ambani International School, the American School of Bombay and Ascend International School among others, and this planned district holds the densest cluster of IB schools in India. For MYP families that density has a specific benefit: tutors who work this area are inside the International Baccalaureate rather than spreading across several boards, so a tutor who genuinely knows criterion marking is findable without going outside the belt. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Dhirubhai Ambani International School, the American School of Bombay, Ascend International School or any other school named on this page. Schools are named because their reporting formats and assessment calendars differ, even within this cluster, and that is what decides how a comment should be read. Ask which school first. A tutor who has seen the same format for other students will interpret a band comment faster and more accurately than one meeting it for the first time.

The MYP calendar has a quieter pressure pattern than the Diploma one, and it misleads parents. Because there are no public examinations in most years, the assessment load looks lighter. It is not: criterion-marked tasks arrive through the year, each one counting, and a student who treats three of them casually has set their grade before the final term. The practical consequence is that MYP home classes across Mumbai work best booked steadily through a year rather than urgently in the month a report lands.

sections.heading: MYP home tuition in Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC), or online?
paragraphs: For this age group home tuition is the clear default and the gap between modes is wider than it is for older students. A tutor at the table can see a thirteen year old stop concentrating, redirect without making it a confrontation, and insist on written planning before writing begins. On a screen most of that disappears. An IB MYP home tutor in Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) sitting alongside the work also gets to watch the student attempt something unaided, which is the only reliable way to tell understanding from recall at this age.

Online has a narrower but real role. An IB online tutor in Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) is useful for a scarce language acquisition pairing, for a short session reviewing a draft before submission, or during a stretch when a family is travelling and the alternative is a four-week gap. It can also work well for a mature Year 5 student who is already self-managing, since they are closer to Diploma working habits than to Year 2 ones.

The honest trade-offs are blunt at this age. A screen session with the camera on a child's face teaches very little, because the work is invisible and the attention is unverifiable. A younger child will also quietly stop writing while appearing to listen. If online is the only option, insist on a camera over the page and on written work submitted afterwards, and expect progress to be slower than it would be in person. For most MYP students the right answer is a weekly visit with online used only as a fallback.

Ask how they handle a student who will not engage, since at this age that is a more common obstacle than lack of ability. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because criterion bands depend on tasks nobody has seen yet. sections.heading: The personal project in Year 5 and the step that follows it
paragraphs: The personal project is a sustained independent piece of work in the final MYP year, and it is the first time most students manage a long timeline alone. The failures are rarely about ability. A goal is set so broadly that no evidence of progress is possible. The process journal is written in one weekend near the end, so the reflection has nothing real to reflect on. The product is finished and the report is rushed, when it is the report that carries the assessment. Students who treat the journal as a running record from week one find the rest straightforward.

A tutor's role here is coaching rather than content. They can question whether the goal is specific enough to be evidenced, help build a timeline with checkpoints that a fifteen year old can actually meet, ask the questions that turn a vague reflection into a concrete one, and read the report against the criteria. They should not choose the project, make the product or write the reflection, and a tutor who offers to is creating an academic honesty problem the student will own alone.

The same habits decide how the move into senior school goes. The Diploma Programme assumes a student can plan long written work, keep a record as they go, and produce a draft before the deadline week. Those are exactly the personal project habits. This is why the most valuable Year 5 tutoring is often not subject teaching at all, and why MYP support booked in Year 5 pays off in the first Diploma term. sections.heading: What four weeks of MYP home classes in Mumbai should change
paragraphs: Expect changes in how work is produced rather than in a band. A plan written before an answer is started. A hypothesis stated so that it could actually be tested. A conclusion that quotes the student's own results. An analysis paragraph that names a technique and its effect instead of retelling the story. You should also have a one-sentence account of which criterion was costing your child marks and why. If after a month nobody has looked at the task sheets, the sessions are revising content and the bands will not move.

Across a term the band change usually arrives, and it arrives unevenly: the criterion that was explicitly taught improves first, and the others follow as the habit generalises. Progress at this age is also more sensitive to engagement than to teaching hours, which is why we ask how a tutor handles a reluctant student. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and in the MYP that is especially true because bands depend on tasks that have not been set yet and on how a particular teacher applies the criteria.

The limits are worth stating. A home tutor for MYP subject groups in Mumbai cannot make a student care, cannot sit the assessed task, and cannot undo a year of casually completed work in a month. What tutoring can do is teach the specific intellectual moves each criterion rewards, which is a smaller and more achievable job than most families imagine when they first read a report. The students who move fastest are the ones who bring the task sheet to the session instead of leaving it at school.

faqs.question: What does a comment about criterion C on the report actually mean?
faqs.answer: It depends on the subject group, which is why the letters confuse parents. Criterion C in Mathematics is communicating, in Sciences it is processing and evaluating, and in Language and Literature it is producing text. Each rewards a different intellectual move. Bring the report and the task sheet to the first session and a tutor who has taught the group will tell you within minutes which move was missing. faqs.question: My son is bright but his MYP bands are average. How is that possible?
faqs.answer: Because criterion marking rewards specific moves rather than knowledge. A student can understand the topic thoroughly and still score mid-band by describing where the criterion asks them to analyse, or by finding a pattern without generalising and justifying it. This is the most common MYP situation we see and it is good news, because the fix is teachable in weeks rather than months. It is not a signal about ability and it is usually not a signal about the teacher either.

faqs.question: Should we start tutoring in MYP or wait for the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: If there is a specific criterion problem, deal with it now, because the habits compound. A student who never learns to plan before writing in Year 4 does not suddenly acquire it in the first Diploma term, when the workload leaves no room to learn it. Waiting is defensible when the bands are solid and the only concern is general ambition. Where a report keeps naming the same criterion across two terms, that is a pattern rather than a bad week.

faqs.question: How much help is allowed with the personal project?

A tutor can question whether the goal is specific enough to evidence, help build a realistic timeline with checkpoints, push for the process journal to be kept weekly, and read the report against the criteria. They must not choose the project, make the product or write the reflection. faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one subject group?

faqs.question: My daughter refuses to engage with a tutor. What then?
faqs.answer: Tell us before the first session, because it changes who we shortlist. sections.heading: MYP Years 1 to 5: what the programme is actually asking for
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme (MYP) runs for five years between the Primary Years Programme (PYP) and the Diploma Programme (DP), covering roughly the ages at which children in other systems meet middle school and early senior school. It is organised around eight subject groups: language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, arts, physical and health education, and design. Every student studies all eight for most of the programme, which is a wider spread than any national curriculum asks for and is the single biggest source of workload complaints we hear from parents in Mumbai.

What the programme assesses is not content recall. Each subject is marked against four published criteria with descriptors, so a student receives a level per criterion rather than a percentage, and those levels are converted into a subject grade using boundaries the school applies. The practical effect is that two students who know exactly the same chemistry can receive very different science grades, because one can design an investigation and evaluate a method and the other cannot. Ask your school's coordinator how levels are converted for your child's year, since that process is set by the programme and applied locally.

Around the subject work sit three structural elements parents hear about and rarely get explained. Approaches to Learning are the explicit skills the programme teaches alongside content, covering research, communication, self-management, thinking and social skills, and they appear in criterion descriptors. Interdisciplinary units ask students to combine two subject groups on one task, which is a particular shock to students who compartmentalise. Service as Action runs through the programme as a participation requirement rather than an assessed subject.

The programme ends with the personal project in MYP Year 5: a self-directed piece of work where the student sets a goal, keeps a process journal, produces an outcome and writes a report on it. It is assessed on the quality of the planning, the application of skills and the honesty of the reflection, not on how impressive the product looks. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with any school named here and not affiliated with the IB Organization, and we do not guarantee grades.

sections.heading: The eight subject groups, and what criteria A to D mean in each
paragraphs: The four criteria are differently named in every subject group, and that is where most parent confusion starts. In mathematics they cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In sciences they cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In language and literature they cover analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. In language acquisition they are simply listening, reading, speaking and writing.

In individuals and societies the four are knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating, and thinking critically. In design they are inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution, and evaluating. In the arts they run through investigating, developing, creating or performing, and evaluating. In physical and health education they cover knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting on and improving performance. Reading that list carefully explains most low grades: only one criterion in each subject is about knowing things.

The patterns that follow are consistent and useful. A student who scores well on the first criterion everywhere and badly on the others is a content learner who has not been taught process, and that is the most fixable profile there is. A student weak on communicating across several subjects has a notation and structure problem, not a subject problem, and one tutor can address it in all of them. A student weak on the critical or evaluative criterion is usually writing what happened rather than judging it, which is a specific writing skill. MYP subject groups home classes Borivali East families book most often turn out to be about one of those three profiles.

Mathematics deserves a separate note because it is the most requested subject group here. The investigating patterns criterion asks a student to find a rule, generalise it in symbols, test the generalisation and justify it. Children who can execute every calculation often freeze there, because nobody has told them that guessing a pattern and then proving it is the expected method rather than cheating. Six to eight weeks of structured investigation work usually moves the level, and it is also direct preparation for the Diploma Programme mathematical exploration later. IB MYP home tuition in Borivali East that targets a named criterion is measurably easier to evaluate than general support.

sections.heading: How do you read an MYP report card from a Mumbai school?
paragraphs: Read across the criteria before you read the grade. An MYP report gives a level for each of four criteria per subject and then a subject grade derived from them, and the grade hides the information you need. Two students with the same science grade can have opposite problems: one strong on knowing and understanding and weak on inquiring and designing, the other the reverse. The first needs investigation practice, the second needs content. A tutor hired without that distinction will spend a term on the wrong half.

Then look across subjects for the repeated criterion. If communicating is the lowest level in mathematics, in sciences and in individuals and societies, you do not have three subject problems. You have one presentation and structure problem appearing in three places, and one tutor can address all three at once. The same logic applies to the critical or evaluative criterion: a student who scores low on thinking critically in humanities and on reflecting in sciences is writing description where judgement is wanted.

Read the comments for process language rather than content language. MYP teacher comments tend to name the skill: works well with support and needs to plan independently, or produces accurate work and does not explain reasoning, or participates well and submits process journals late. Those sentences are the actual brief for a tutor, far more than the grade is. Keep the reports from two consecutive terms side by side, because a criterion that has not moved in two reporting cycles is the one to spend money on.

The schools in this catchment set the rhythm. Families here mostly attend JBCN International School, Borivali, which runs IB and IGCSE pathways and draws from Borivali East and Borivali West, or Singapore International School at Dahisar East, an IB school taking children from Dahisar and the northern end of this area. Some families at the southern edge attend schools in Kandivali East. We name them because their reporting cycles and personal project deadlines decide when tuition is useful. IB Gram has no relationship with any of these schools.

sections.heading: Home classes or online for a Middle Years student in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home, and for this age group it is not a close call. A Middle Years student is in the years where independent working habits are still being built, and the value of a tutor at the same table is largely supervisory: noticing that the student has stopped, that the process journal has not been opened, that the question was read once and misunderstood. A screen hides all of that. Online is the wrong choice for a Year 2 or Year 3 student who cannot yet work alone, however convenient the scheduling looks.

There are two honest exceptions. A language acquisition tutor for a less commonly taught language may simply not live within reach, and an IB online tutor in Borivali East is far better than no specialist at all, particularly for the speaking and listening criteria which work acceptably on a call. The second is the personal project in MYP Year 5, where a short screen session to review a process journal entry or a draft report is efficient and does not need anyone to travel.

Hybrid works from around MYP Year 4 onwards, once the student can be trusted to work between sessions. One home evening carries the teaching and the habit-building, and a short online slot handles the specific question that came up mid-week. Below that year group, the online half tends to become a supervised homework call, which is not a bad thing but should be priced and described as what it is rather than as tuition.

There is one more reason to prefer home classes at this stage, and it is about the parent rather than the child. A tutor in your flat can show you, in two minutes at the end of a session, exactly what the criterion descriptor asks for and where your child's work falls short of it. That conversation changes how a parent reads the next report, and it does not happen over a screen. Families who get that explanation once stop needing to ask what the levels mean.

sections.heading: What to check in an MYP tutor, beyond the subject in Mumbai
paragraphs: IB Gram verifies identity against a government photo document, the subject qualification at the level claimed, teaching experience probed by programme and by criterion rather than by job title, and references where the tutor has previously worked with families. Your own check runs on the free discovery call and it is unusually easy here, because the report gives you the material. Send it in advance. And be wary of anyone who dismisses the criteria as box-ticking, because the grade is built from them and a tutor who disagrees with the programme is not going to raise the levels. sections.heading: Will my child cope with the jump from MYP to the Diploma Programme?
paragraphs: Usually yes, with one specific piece of preparation, and the thing to prepare is not content. The Middle Years Programme marks against criteria over extended tasks with support and redrafting. The Diploma Programme marks timed written answers against mark schemes built on command terms, with no redrafting and no support. A student who has spent five years producing considered, reflective, well-presented work can lose two grades in the first DP term purely because the output has changed shape, and that reads at home like a collapse when it is a format mismatch.

The repair is six to eight weeks of timed answer practice, ideally in the gap between MYP Year 5 and the start of DP1, and it is the highest-value tuition money a family in this catchment can spend. The skills are specific: reading a command term and matching the answer's length and type to it, writing under time without planning for ten minutes first, showing working and reasoning in a form a marker can follow quickly, and accepting a first draft as the only draft. None of that is hard. It is simply new, and nobody teaches it because it falls between two programmes.

The second part of the transition is choice, and it gets made in a hurry at the end of MYP Year 5. Three Higher Level and three Standard Level subjects, mapped from the eight subject groups the student has been doing, plus the mathematics route decision between the analysis-led and applications-led courses. The mathematics decision is the one families most often get wrong, because it is made on current comfort rather than on what the student's likely university courses expect. Check the published entry requirements of three or four real universities before deciding, not afterwards.

The third part is workload literacy. Diploma Programme students carry Internal Assessment (IA) coursework in most subjects plus the Extended Essay (EE) and Theory of Knowledge (TOK), and all of that lands in the same autumn. A student who learned to plan during the personal project is in a far better position than one who produced it in a fortnight. That is the real reason the personal project matters, and it is a decent argument for taking it seriously rather than treating it as an extra. Families booking IB MYP home classes in Borivali East in Year 5 should raise the transition explicitly on the first call, because it changes what the sessions do. sections.heading: What eight weeks of MYP home tuition should change
paragraphs: A criterion level, if the work was targeted, and a set of habits regardless. The habits come first and a parent can see them in the exercise book: the student plans before writing instead of starting at the top of the page, states a rule in general terms rather than listing examples, labels and annotates work without being asked, and can say what the task is being assessed on. Those four are visible within six sessions of starting home tuition in Mumbai. If none of them has appeared, raise it at the fortnightly review.

Over a reporting cycle the level should move on the targeted criterion, and that is a cleaner measure than any percentage. This is one real advantage of criterion marking for a family paying for tuition: the thing you asked for is reported on separately. If communicating was the target and communicating has not moved after a full cycle, either the plan was wrong or the work was not done, and a good tutor will say which.

Across the whole programme the realistic picture is that broad, low-level weakness takes longer than a single criterion gap and is more worth fixing. A Year 2 student who learns to plan, investigate and present will carry that into every subject and into the Diploma Programme years later. A Year 5 student eight weeks from the personal project deadline can be helped with structure and reflection and cannot be given a different project. We will tell you which situation you are in before taking the booking.

IB Gram does not guarantee grades and publishes no success rates, because any figure we printed would be unverifiable. What we commit to is a written note every two to four weeks naming the criterion worked on, what changed and what did not. Two vague notes in a row is the signal to ask for a different tutor. faqs.question: My child's MYP report shows levels, not percentages. How do I tell whether that is good?
faqs.answer: Read across the four criteria before you look at the subject grade. The grade is derived from the criterion levels and conceals the pattern you need. A student strong on knowing and understanding and weak on investigating has a process problem; one with the reverse pattern has a content problem; one who is level with themselves across all four is simply behind. Then look across subjects for the same low criterion repeating, because that is one transferable weakness rather than three subject failures. Communicating covers notation, structure, labelling and showing reasoning in a form a reader can follow, and it is the criterion most students have never been explicitly taught. It shows up as a low level in several subjects at once, which is how you can tell it is a skill rather than a subject gap. sections.heading: MYP Years 1 to 5: what actually changes each year?
paragraphs: The framework stays the same and the demands rise steeply, which is why a student can hold steady levels for two years and then slip. The Middle Years Programme runs across five years, and across that span the same criteria are applied with rising expectations: a generalisation that earned a good level in year one earns a mediocre one in year four, with no change in the wording of the criterion. Parents reading two reports side by side often conclude the child has gone backwards when the band descriptors were simply applied to older students.

Years one and two are where habits are cheap to build and almost nobody builds them. Writing a conclusion that refers to the data. Defining a term before using it. Controlling one variable at a time. Showing a method before an answer. Those four habits cost nothing to install at eleven or twelve and are expensive to install at fifteen, when the student has four years of being rewarded for enthusiastic description behind them. This is the strongest argument for starting IB MYP home tuition in Borivali West early rather than at the first crisis.

Years three and four are when the subject groups separate properly and the workload becomes real. Students meet interdisciplinary units, Approaches to Learning (ATL) skills get reported on explicitly, and Service as Action expectations sit alongside academic tasks. A student who is organised survives this comfortably; a disorganised one with good subject understanding starts handing work in late and losing levels on criteria that had nothing to do with their understanding. Most of the home tuition we arrange in Mumbai for these two years is about structure rather than subject content. A good tutor treats that as a real academic problem rather than a parenting one.

The final MYP year carries the personal project and the first serious thought about the Diploma Programme (DP). Some schools enter students for MYP eAssessment with on-screen examinations and ePortfolios and some do not, which changes the final year substantially, so confirm what your school actually does rather than assuming. Whatever the answer, the final year is where the gap between criterion-based success and examination-based success becomes visible, and it is the gap that the next two years will test hard.

sections.heading: The eight subject groups and what criteria A to D reward
paragraphs: There are eight subject groups: Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design. Each is marked against four criteria labelled A to D, and the names behind those letters differ by subject. In Mathematics they run from knowing and understanding, through investigating patterns and communicating, to applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In Sciences they cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The letters look identical on a report card and ask for completely different work.

That mismatch is the single commonest cause of a confusing MYP result. A student in Mathematics who is strong on criterion A and weak on criterion B is not bad at mathematics; they can use techniques and cannot investigate a pattern, generalise it and justify the generalisation. A student in Sciences who scores well on criterion A and poorly on criterion B can recall content and cannot design a controlled investigation. A student in Language and Literature can write fluently, score well on producing text, and lose heavily on analysis because they described what happened rather than examining how the writer achieved it.

Criterion D is where the most marks are quietly lost across every subject group, because it asks for something schools rarely teach explicitly. In Sciences it wants the impacts of science discussed with reference to sources. In Mathematics it wants mathematics applied to a real context, with the limitations of the model acknowledged. In Individuals and Societies it wants critical thinking, meaning different interpretations weighed rather than a summary presented. A student who writes a competent account and no evaluation will score respectably on three criteria and poorly on the fourth, every time.

This is why a MYP subject groups tutor in Borivali West should start with the task sheet rather than the textbook. The sheet names which strands are being assessed, and often a task assesses only two of the four criteria. Teaching the whole topic when the task assesses investigating and communicating is wasted effort. Confirm the current criterion names, strand wording and grade boundaries with your child's subject teacher, because the IB revises subject guides on its own cycle and older versions circulate widely online.

The second question is about the process journal and the organisation problem, because it separates people who treat MYP seriously from people who treat it as easy teaching. sections.heading: The personal project and the MYP to DP transition
paragraphs: The personal project in the final Middle Years Programme year is the piece most students underestimate and most parents misunderstand. It is not primarily a product. The student sets a goal, works towards an outcome, keeps a process journal as they go, and writes a report assessed against its own criteria, with a supervisor at school overseeing the work. The journal is where it goes wrong: students treat it as paperwork to be assembled at the end, and a reconstructed journal cannot show the decision-making and adjustment the criteria are looking for.

What a tutor can legitimately do here is narrow and useful. They can help your child interrogate whether the goal is specific enough to be achievable, teach them to record decisions as they happen rather than afterwards, read a draft report for structure and clarity, and insist that the reflection discusses what changed and why. They may not choose the goal, make the product or write the report. Your child signs an academic honesty declaration, and a supervisor who has read the journal weekly will notice work that does not match it.

The MYP to Diploma Programme transition is what actually worries parents here, and the worry is reasonable. A student who has done well on criteria has been rewarded for inquiry, process and communication, and the Diploma Programme will ask for correct answers under timed conditions, Higher Level and Standard Level choices, an Internal Assessment in most subjects, an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. Those are not the same skills. A strong MYP record does not predict a strong first Diploma Programme term, and families who assume it does get a shock in the first set of tests.

The fix is to spend the final MYP year building the things the programme does not test directly: timed practice, writing under pressure, accuracy with numbers and units, and reading an unfamiliar question to work out what it wants. A tutor running MYP home classes in Mumbai can do that alongside the criterion work without disrupting it, and it is the single best use of that year. Parents hunting for the best IB tutor in Borivali West for this stage should be asking who has moved students across that bridge, not who has the longest subject résumé.

A student weak on investigating patterns who is now generalising and justifying should show it there, while knowing and understanding stays where it was. That is success, and parents sometimes read it as partial failure because the headline subject grade only shifted a little. Those transfer across every subject group and into the Diploma Programme afterwards. What no tutor can do is make a student who hands nothing in on time score well on criteria that measure process.

paragraphs: Four things make the first call productive. The MYP year your child is in. The subject group, and which criteria dropped. The most recent task sheet with the marked work attached. And two weekly slots chosen honestly around school transport, sport and the fact that a 6.30pm start means the tutor leaves home at 5.45pm. faqs.question: I cannot understand my child's MYP report card. What do the numbers mean?
faqs.answer: Each subject reports levels against four criteria labelled A to D, and the subject grade on the one to seven scale is derived from those levels using published boundaries. There is no percentage, so converting the numbers in your head will mislead you. Read the criterion names rather than the letters, because the same letter means different things in different subjects. Then read the Approaches to Learning comments, which often explain the levels. Ask your school for the current boundaries rather than using a figure from an older document, since these are revised.

faqs.question: My child writes well but scores low on criterion A. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always because they described rather than analysed. In Language and Literature, analysis asks how a writer achieves an effect, not what happens; in Individuals and Societies it asks for interpretations weighed against each other. Fluent, confident writing that retells the content scores respectably on producing text and poorly on analysing. The fix is structural rather than linguistic: one claim, one piece of evidence, one explanation of how the evidence supports the claim, repeated. Most students can do this within a few weeks once somebody names the problem precisely.

faqs.question: Can an IB MYP home tutor in Borivali West help with the personal project?
faqs.answer: Yes, within clear limits. A tutor can press your child on whether the goal is specific enough to achieve, teach them to record decisions in the process journal as they happen instead of reconstructing it later, read a draft report for structure and clarity, and insist the reflection explains what changed and why. A tutor may not choose the goal, make the product or write the report. Your child signs an academic honesty declaration, and a school supervisor reading the journal weekly will notice work that does not match it.

faqs.question: Does MYP tutoring mean one tutor for all eight subject groups?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who offers that is selling availability. The eight subject groups are Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design, and no one person teaches all of them to a useful standard. What does transfer is criterion literacy: a tutor strong in one subject group can teach your child how to read a task sheet and write an evaluation, and those habits carry across. Pick one or two subjects that matter and do them properly.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Borivali West depend on at MYP level?
faqs.answer: Subject group, how scarce that subject is locally, travel distance, session length, and whether the tutor reads drafts between sessions. MYP tutoring generally costs less per hour than Higher Level Diploma Programme work, because there is no exam-standard marking involved, though personal project supervision and draft reading add real time. faqs.question: How does my building's gate protocol affect a weekly MYP session?
faqs.answer: It decides whether the session starts on time, which matters a great deal for a younger student. Most buildings in Borivali West register visitors at the gate, and a tutor phoned up and cleared individually every week will lose ten minutes a visit. Ask your society office whether a standing weekly entry can be recorded against the tutor's name and number for the term. Tell us the arrangement during the brief, because a tutor who knows the protocol plans their travel around it instead of discovering it at the barrier.

faqs.question: Is online tutoring suitable for an MYP student?
faqs.answer: Rarely as the whole arrangement, and we would rather say so. Eleven to sixteen is the age group least able to work unsupervised for ninety minutes, and most MYP difficulties are about process: an unread task sheet, an empty process journal, work started the night before. A tutor at the table sees all of that; a screen does not. Online works well for two narrower jobs: a language nobody local teaches, and a short mid-week check that a task has actually been started. Hybrid built that way holds up.

faqs.question: How soon will criterion levels improve?
faqs.answer: Not within four weeks, because levels only change when the next summative task is assessed. What should change in four weeks is visible in the exercise book and the folder: the task sheet annotated before work begins, command terms underlined, a plan with dated stages, conclusions referring to evidence. By the next reporting cycle, expect the specific criteria that were targeted to move while the others hold steady. Agree which two criteria the tutor is working on at the start, and judge them against that list rather than the subject grade.

faqs.question: What if the MYP tutor is not the right fit?

faqs.question: Will MYP success predict how my child does in the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and this is the most useful thing a parent can know early. The Middle Years Programme rewards inquiry, process and communication assessed against criteria; the Diploma Programme asks for accurate answers under timed conditions alongside an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge. A student with strong criterion levels can still struggle in the first Diploma Programme term. The final MYP year is the right time to build timed practice, accuracy with numbers and units, and the skill of reading an unfamiliar question. We do not guarantee grades in either programme.

sections.heading: The eight MYP subject groups, and which ones parents call about
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme (MYP) is organised into eight subject groups: language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, arts, physical and health education, and design. Running across them are the approaches to learning skills, service as action, and at least one interdisciplinary unit, with the personal project arriving in the final year. Each unit is framed by a key concept, related concepts and a global context, and that framing is not decoration: the assessment task will ask the student to use it, and a student who ignores the statement of inquiry loses bands for reasons the content revision never addresses.

In practice, families in this pocket call about four of the eight. Mathematics, because the investigating patterns criterion asks students to generalise and justify, which no amount of practice sums prepares them for. Language and literature, because analysis is a learned skill and most students arrive able only to retell. Sciences, because designing an investigation and evaluating data are marked separately from knowing the science. And design, because it is the subject most often treated as low-stakes by students and marked seriously by teachers, which produces a nasty surprise in the second term.

Language acquisition is the quiet one. A student who was placed in a phase that is slightly too easy coasts for two years and then struggles the moment the Diploma Programme asks for real production in that language. A student in a phase slightly too hard loses bands for language use regardless of ideas. If a report shows strong comprehension and weak production, that is worth a conversation with the school about phase placement before it is worth tuition.

A note on scope, because parents reasonably ask. This page is about the Middle Years Programme specifically. Diploma Programme subject choices, Higher Level decisions and the International General Certificate of Secondary Education pathway are separate questions and we have separate pages for them. What belongs here is the programme your child is in now, the criteria they are marked against, and the Year 5 project that is about to land. On the platform a listing shows as an MYP subject groups IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai entry, which just means the tutor is cleared across those years; the subject-group experience is written underneath.

sections.heading: What criteria A to D actually reward
paragraphs: Every Middle Years Programme subject is assessed against four criteria, and each criterion asks for a different kind of performance. In mathematics the four cover knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In sciences they cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In language and literature they cover analysing, organising, producing text, and using language. The content knowledge a parent thinks of as the subject sits almost entirely inside the first criterion. Three quarters of the marking is about what the student does with it.

That is the single most useful thing to understand about the programme. A child who knows the material and is marked in the middle is usually losing the other three criteria, and no amount of revision touches them. Investigating patterns wants a general rule, a justification and ideally a test of the rule against a new case, so a student who spots the pattern and stops has done perhaps half the task. Communicating wants correct notation, labelled diagrams and a readable structure. Applying in real-life contexts wants interpretation and a judgement about whether the answer is sensible, which students skip because the maths felt finished.

In language and literature the gap is analysis against summary, and it is the most common single problem we are asked about. A student writes what happened in the text, perhaps very fluently, and the criterion wanted why the writer made a choice and what effect it produces. Fixing it is a technique job, not a reading job: a few sessions on quotation selection, on the sentence pattern that links a choice to an effect, and on cutting narration out of a paragraph. MYP subject groups home classes Breach Candy families book for this reason often show a visible change in one marked task.

Each criterion is marked in bands against descriptors, and your school converts the four criterion results into a single subject grade using a published boundary scheme. Ask the school for that scheme. Parents spend terms guessing at what a band means when the conversion table answers it in a minute, and a tutor who has seen it can tell you which single criterion is costing the grade. It is the first document we ask for when IB MYP home tuition in Breach Candy is being set up.

paragraphs: Children in this pocket are concentrated in a few schools, and the way each reports progress differs more than parents expect. Bombay International School at Babulnath and Activity High School on Peddar Road are the two that come up in almost every Breach Candy conversation, and families also consider Aditya Birla World Academy at Tardeo, Ecole Mondiale World School at Juhu and Oberoi International School for the Middle Years Programme years. The reporting itself is the first source of confusion. Some schools report a band per criterion per subject, some report a converted subject grade, some report both, and the conversion boundaries are set locally. A parent comparing a child at one school with a cousin at another is comparing two different scales, which produces a great deal of unnecessary worry at family dinners across South Mumbai. Ask your school for the boundary scheme and for the task-specific clarifications. Those two documents answer most of what parents try to work out by inference.

The Year 5 step into the Diploma Programme is the thing that actually worries families, and the worry is well placed. The Middle Years Programme rewards process, reflection and investigation, and it is generous about the route a student takes to an answer. The Diploma Programme is far more exacting about precision: definitions have required forms, mathematics demands fluency rather than exploration, and written work is marked against criteria that assume academic register. A student who has coasted on ideas and personality can meet a wall in the first term of DP1. The Year 5 work that prevents it is unglamorous: accurate written definitions, arithmetic and algebraic fluency, proper referencing, note-taking that produces usable notes, and the habit of starting work more than a day before it is due.

The assessment calendar matters too. Middle Years Programme units run in blocks, so a child can have two summative tasks in one week and nothing for a fortnight. Ask for the unit plan dates at the start of term. A tutor who knows a summative task is coming in ten days can prepare for it. A tutor who hears about it the evening before can only sympathise.

sections.heading: Is home tuition better than online for an MYP child in Mumbai?
paragraphs: For a younger Middle Years Programme child, almost always yes, and the reason is attention rather than pedagogy. An eleven or twelve-year-old working on a screen at five in the afternoon is one notification away from gone, and the tutor cannot see it happen. In the room, a tutor can close the laptop, put the task sheet on the table, and keep a child working for fifty minutes who would have lasted fifteen online. Home tuition also lets the tutor see the workspace and the school bag, and a disorganised bag explains more about missing summative tasks than any report does.

There is a second reason specific to this programme. Middle Years Programme tasks are often produced on a school platform with a rubric attached, and a tutor sitting beside the student can walk through the clarification sheet with them, point at the strand being lost, and have the student fix the paragraph while the comment is still fresh. Doing that over a call works and takes longer, because the student has to drive the screen while listening.

Online still has real uses, and for older Middle Years Programme students it becomes genuinely competitive. A short screen-share two nights before a summative task, with the rubric open, is efficient. Through the heaviest monsoon weeks it keeps continuity. When the subject group is unusual, say a specific language acquisition phase, an IB online tutor in Breach Candy who actually teaches that language beats a nearer generalist. And for marking written work, comments in a shared document get reread in a way pencil notes do not.

The honest costs. An IB private tutor Breach Candy parents bring into the flat carries travel in the price, and for a Middle Years Programme child that is usually money well spent because attention is the scarce resource. Online is cheaper and demands self-management that most twelve-year-olds have not built yet. Hybrid, one visit plus a short mid-week check, works well from Year 4 onwards and less well before that. We will say which we would pick and then do what you decide.

sections.heading: What should you ask before an MYP tutor starts home classes?
paragraphs: We check identity, the subjects and year groups the person has genuinely taught, their history with the International Baccalaureate, and references we have actually spoken to. sections.heading: Does the personal project really need a tutor?
paragraphs: Usually not in the way parents imagine, and sometimes badly. The personal project arrives in the final Middle Years Programme year and is assessed on the process as much as on the thing produced: the planning, the application of skills, and the reflection, all evidenced through a process journal and a report. Students almost universally get this backwards. They make the product first, enjoy making it, and then try to reconstruct a journal afterwards, which reads exactly as reconstructed and loses marks for the criteria that were supposed to be the point.

So the useful intervention is early and small. Someone needs to sit with the student in the first fortnight and establish three habits: write in the journal the same day something happens, including the things that went wrong; keep every source with a reference at the moment it is used rather than at the end; and define the goal narrowly enough that success and failure are both visible. A project to raise awareness about marine plastic is unmarkable. A project to design and test a reusable packaging prototype for one named use is markable, because you can say whether it worked.

A tutor must not make the product, write the journal, or draft the report. That is not a cautious reading of the rules; it is the rule, and your school supervises the project precisely to check it. What a tutor legitimately does is ask questions. Why that goal. What will you count as evidence. Which skill are you actually developing here and how will you show it. What went wrong this week and what did you change. Those questions, asked weekly for twenty minutes, are worth more than any amount of help with the making, and they are the most defensible use of IB MYP home classes in Breach Candy during the project year.

The honest reason many families want help is time rather than ability. The personal project lands in a year that also carries summative tasks across eight subject groups and, in many schools here, the first serious conversations about Diploma Programme subject choices. A student with weak planning habits loses the project in the diary before they lose it in the marking. If that is your situation, the tutor you want is one who will protect twenty minutes a week for the journal, not one who will produce an impressive outcome.

One more thing worth saying because it is rarely said. A modest, well-documented, honestly reflected project is marked better than an ambitious one with a thin journal. Students and parents both find that counter-intuitive, and it is the most useful sentence on this page.

sections.heading: What should change after four weeks with an MYP tutor?
paragraphs: Four weeks in, the changes should be visible in the student work rather than in the report, which will not have been reissued. Specifically: one marked task where the previously lost criterion is better, a set of notes that somebody could revise from, a task started more than a day before the deadline, and the ability to tell you in their own words what criterion is being assessed in the current unit. That last one is the best single test available to a parent and takes thirty seconds. If your child cannot say what the task is marked on, the tutor has been teaching the subject and not the programme.

At one term, expect the criterion profile to even out before the converted grade moves. A student who was strong on knowing and understanding and weak on the other three does not jump a grade by improving one criterion slightly; they move when two of the three come up together, which takes a term of marked tasks. Teacher comments shift last. This lag causes real friction in households here, because a parent who has paid for a term wants the report to say something different and the report is built from tasks set before the change happened.

There is a specific Middle Years Programme caution. Criterion bands move in jumps, not smoothly, because each task samples different strands. A single task result is noisy. Look at three marked tasks in the same subject before concluding anything, and ignore the one outlier that caused the panic.

Our limits. Tutoring adds leverage to the work a child does, and for a Middle Years Programme student the largest gains are usually in habits rather than in content: planning, note-taking, reading the rubric, starting early. Those are slower to show and more durable. We do not guarantee grades or bands, we do not publish success rates, and we will not tell you that one weekly hour substitutes for a child who has not opened the task sheet. What we commit to is an honest answer at two to four weeks, including when the answer is that this match is not working.
