sections.heading: Which of the eight subject groups actually need a tutor?
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme covers Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design. Across that spread, three patterns account for most of the tutoring that genuinely helps. The first is Mathematics, where the criterion about investigating patterns reliably exposes students who compute accurately and cannot generalise or justify. They are not weak at mathematics; they have never been taught to express a pattern in symbols, test it on a new case and explain why it holds. One properly worked example at the required band teaches more than a term of extra practice.

The second is Language and Literature, where the criteria separate analysis from summary and where most mid-band work is summary wearing analytical vocabulary. A student describing what a writer does, without saying what effect it creates and how the technique produces it, will sit in the same band for two years regardless of how much they read. This is a structural fix and a tutor can teach it with two annotated paragraphs. Language Acquisition behaves differently: the assessed skills are receptive and productive, and the common failure is a student with good vocabulary who has never practised the specific task formats.

The third is Sciences and Individuals and Societies, where the investigation and critical-thinking criteria do the damage. In Sciences, a student who knows the content loses marks because they cannot formulate a testable question, identify variables or evaluate a method. In Individuals and Societies, they lose marks because sources are described rather than interrogated for origin, purpose and limitation. Arts, Physical and Health Education and Design are rarely tutored and are occasionally where a child's grade is actually being lost, usually on process documentation rather than on the work itself. MYP subject groups home classes Santacruz East families book should start from the criteria sheet, not from the textbook, whichever group it is. That is the one instruction we give every IB MYP home tutor in Santacruz East before a first session.

sections.heading: The Mumbai school year an MYP family plans around
paragraphs: Children from Santacruz East attend schools in several directions, and in the MYP the school's own assessment design matters more than anywhere else in the IB, because the tasks are set internally. Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC sits a short run across the highway. Bombay Cambridge International School in Andheri East is up the line. Others travel to schools in Santacruz and Juhu. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of them; we name them because their internal task calendars, reporting cycles and personal project deadlines are what decide which weeks are hard in your flat.

The MYP year in Mumbai has a shape worth knowing. June and July are quiet, and they are the best months to fix reading, writing or mathematical fluency because no assessed task is due. August and September bring the first marked tasks of the year and the first criteria sheets, which is when most enquiries arrive and when they should. October and November carry the heaviest task load across several subject groups at once, and in Year 5 the personal project milestones land in the same stretch. The new year brings the second reporting cycle, and the spring is where Year 5 students make DP subject choices.

The practical consequence for a family is that MYP pressure is distributed rather than concentrated, which is why it is so often missed. There is no single examination to point at, so a child can drift at mid-band for two years without any week feeling like a crisis. The useful discipline is to read the criteria sheets each reporting cycle and look for a criterion that is weak in more than one subject group, because that is a skill problem rather than a subject problem and it is the single highest-value thing a tutor can be pointed at. Families running MYP subject groups home classes Santacruz East children need usually start from exactly that observation.

sections.heading: Do MYP home classes work better than online in Mumbai?
paragraphs: For most MYP students, yes, and more clearly than at DP level. The younger the child, the more of the value is presence: an adult at the same table who opens the task sheet, reads the criteria aloud, watches the first ten minutes of independent work and notices that nothing has been written. Attention management on a screen consumes a large share of a session with a Year 1 or Year 2 student, and the habits being built at this stage are physical ones. Sessions at home also let a tutor see the folder, the diary and the organisational chaos that is often the real problem.

Online earns its place in three narrower cases. Language Acquisition conversation practice works well on a screen and sometimes better, because a student speaking to someone outside the household is doing the actual assessed skill. Older MYP students in Years 4 and 5 can use short online sessions productively for draft feedback, especially on analytical writing, which annotates well in a document. And an IB online tutor in Santacruz East may be the only option for a less common language or a specialist Design or Arts need.

If you split the week, keep the home session as the anchor and the online slot for feedback, with one shared folder and notes that carry forward. Ask any candidate how they handle a task sheet remotely, because MYP work depends on the task-specific clarifications the school issues and a tutor who never looks at them is marking against a general standard. The honest trade-off is the same as elsewhere: hybrid saves travel and loses some of the habit correction that only happens when an adult is in the room. For a Year 3 student who cannot start a task without prompting, that correction is the entire purchase, and it is why most MYP home classes in Mumbai stay at the table.

sections.heading: What should you ask an MYP tutor about criteria?
paragraphs: Ask them to explain, for your child's subject group, what separates the band your child is in from the one above, in words a parent can use. A tutor who works in this programme will answer concretely: that the next band requires justification rather than description, or a method with controlled variables rather than a sensible procedure. One who cannot has taught content without reading descriptors, which is the most common gap in the MYP tutoring market. Then ask what the first four sessions will produce, and look for a rewritten task rather than a plan to revise topics.

We check what can be checked remotely: government photo identity, the qualification being claimed, the subject groups and years the tutor will accept, and references from families at the same stage rather than general ones. We also confirm the person on the discovery call is the person who arrives. Your own checks matter more here than at DP level, because MYP teaching quality is harder to judge from a credential and because the student is young enough that rapport does much of the work. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed level or quotes an improvement rate; the marking is internal and criterion-based, and no honest tutor can promise a band.

The practical safeguards are the ordinary ones and they matter more with a younger child. Sessions in a shared room with an adult in the flat, never behind a closed door. Identity shared with your building office before the first visit rather than argued at the gate. A written note after each session naming the task worked on, the criterion targeted and the work set. Payment on the agreed schedule rather than in advance blocks. An IB private tutor Santacruz East families keep across several MYP years nearly always proposed those terms themselves. IB Gram verifies what it can and does not guarantee grades, and in this programme the evidence is the next criteria sheet rather than anyone's word.

sections.heading: Criteria A to D: what a weak criterion is telling you
paragraphs: Each MYP subject is assessed against four criteria, and they are different in every subject group, which is the first thing nobody explains. In Mathematics they run from knowing and understanding, through investigating patterns and communicating, to applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In the Sciences they cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In Language and Literature they cover analysing, organising, producing text and using language. In Individuals and Societies they cover knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. The achievement levels for each are totalled and converted to a subject grade using boundaries your school can give you, and we will not reproduce any of those numbers here because they are revised and because they vary by context.

The diagnostic value sits in the pattern rather than the total. A student strong on the knowledge criterion and weak on the investigation or critical-thinking criterion has a skills gap, not a content gap, and more revision will change nothing. A student weak on communicating across several subject groups has a writing and presentation problem that is cheaper to fix once than to treat four times. A student weak on the first criterion alone genuinely has not learned the material. These three diagnoses lead to completely different tutoring, and the report card looks almost identical in all three cases.

The Year 5 personal project is the clearest example of the same logic. Its marks are not for the product. They are for the goal being specific enough to assess, for the process journal showing genuine decision-making rather than a diary written at the end, for the application of research skills, and for an honest evaluation against the criteria the student set. A project with an impressive outcome and a thin journal scores badly, which surprises families every year. A tutor's legitimate role is to interrogate the goal early, to insist the journal is kept weekly as it happens, and to read the report against the criteria with the student. They must not design the project, make the product or write the report.

Santacruz East is on the highway side, which puts BKC roughly five minutes away and makes it one of the best-value addresses in the Western Suburbs for a family who wants a BKC school without a BKC rent. For MYP families the useful consequence is that the early evening slots a younger child actually needs are reachable, which is not true everywhere in the city. The MYP subject groups in the IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor pool in Mumbai is deep enough that you should be choosing on criteria literacy rather than on availability.

sections.heading: The MYP to DP step, and what progress looks like in Santacruz East
paragraphs: In the first month, the deliverable is one task rewritten to a higher band with the criteria visible, and a sentence you can repeat to the subject teacher about which skill was missing. Not a grade change, because MYP reporting cycles are slow and a tutor claiming movement in four weeks has not seen a new criteria sheet. What should also change is behaviour: your child reading the task sheet and the criteria before starting work, which almost no student does unprompted and which is worth more than any topic revision.

Across a reporting cycle the evidence should be the criteria sheets themselves. The weak criterion moves a band, and ideally the same improvement shows in a second subject group, which is how you know a skill was taught rather than one task rescued. Written work should arrive planned rather than started at the deadline. By Year 5, the personal project journal should exist in real time rather than being reconstructed. If a full cycle has passed with no movement on the targeted criterion, the diagnosis was wrong or the sessions have become homework supervision, and that is worth confronting rather than renewing.

The step into the DP is where honesty matters most. A student with good MYP levels is not automatically ready for DP assessment, because nothing in the MYP tests timed examination technique or sustained independent work against an external deadline. The right Year 5 preparation is timed writing, command terms and one long piece produced without being chased. Our position is unchanged across the programme: IB Gram does not guarantee grades, publishes no success rates, and will say when a tutor is not what a child needs. The best IB tutor in Santacruz East cannot teach a Year 5 student to work independently if every task is still being managed by an adult, and an honest one will tell you that is the real problem.

sections.heading: Starting MYP home tuition in Santacruz East
paragraphs: Four things make the first session productive. The MYP year and subject group in writing. Two marked tasks with the criteria sheets and the teacher's comments, which are the most useful documents you own. The task-specific clarifications the school issued for those tasks, if you have them. And one weekly hour that suits your child's age rather than your diary, which for a younger student means early evening and for a Year 5 student can be later.

Expect session one to be spent reading rather than teaching. The tutor should work through the marked tasks with your child, identify which criterion is costing the most, and explain in plain words what the next band requires. Expect the first month's output to be one rewritten task rather than a syllabus plan, and expect the tutor to say if the honest problem is organisation and reading rather than the subject you called about. That is the most common finding in the MYP and the least welcome one.

Then keep the loop visible: the same weekly hour, a shared folder with tasks and criteria sheets in it, a short note after each session naming the criterion targeted, and a review at four weeks where continuing is a real decision. If the answer is to change the tutor, say so plainly. There is no notice period and no penalty, and we shortlist again from the same corridor. There is also a right time to stop, usually when a student starts planning their own tasks, and we would rather tell you that moment has arrived than keep a booking running. A home tutor for MYP subject groups Mumbai parents hire in Year 3 should be aiming to be unnecessary by Year 5.

faqs.question: My child scores well on the knowledge criterion and badly on another. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the other criterion is testing a skill rather than content. In Mathematics it is usually investigating patterns, which asks the student to generalise, express a rule symbolically and justify it. faqs.question: Is my Year 5 child ready for the Diploma Programme?
faqs.answer: Strong MYP levels are encouraging and they do not answer the question, because nothing in the MYP tests timed examination performance or sustained independent work against an external deadline. Those three can be taught in Year 5 at low cost. Discovering they are missing in the first term of DP1 is considerably more expensive.

faqs.question: Are you affiliated with Dhirubhai Ambani International School or Bombay Cambridge International School?

faqs.answer: More often than at Diploma Programme level, and it depends on what is actually wrong. Where the problem is a skill shared across subjects, such as analytical writing or investigation design, one tutor working on that skill can affect three subject groups at once and is better value than three specialists. Where the problem is genuine content weakness in Mathematics and in a language, split the hire. Ask the candidate which groups they have marked criteria for, not which ones they feel comfortable with.

faqs.question: My child is in MYP Year 2 and is disorganised rather than weak. Is a tutor right?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but hire for the right thing and keep it short. A tutor working on diary use, task planning, reading the criteria before starting and filing work properly can change a Year 2 student's results more than subject teaching will, and should aim to be unnecessary within a term or two. What does not work is an open-ended arrangement that becomes supervised homework for three years. Agree at the outset what the tutor is there to make redundant, then review it honestly.

faqs.question: Does the school's choice of tasks really change what a tutor should do?

MYP assessment is internal, so the school sets the tasks and issues task-specific clarifications that define what each achievement band looks like for that particular piece of work. A tutor who never reads those is marking against a general standard and will give advice that does not match the sheet your child is graded on. Ask the tutor to request them, and send whatever the school has given you before the first session.

faqs.question: How long should MYP home tuition continue?
faqs.answer: Until the skill it was hired for is visible without it, which is usually a term or two for a specific criterion and longer for reading or writing stamina. Put a review at the start of each school year and ask what your child still cannot do alone. The failure mode in this programme is not a bad tutor; it is a reasonable tutor retained for three years because nobody scheduled the conversation. We would rather tell you to stop than keep a weekly slot running out of habit.

sections.heading: MYP Years 1 to 5, and what changes at each stage
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme runs across five years between the Primary Years Programme (PYP) and the Diploma Programme (DP), and parents often treat it as one undifferentiated block. It is not. The early years are closest in feel to the Primary Years Programme: inquiry-led, forgiving, with assessment used mainly to describe where a student is. The middle years are where subject-specific language arrives and where the gap between a student who can discuss an idea and one who can write about it starts to show in the marks. The final years are different again, with the personal project, more demanding criteria descriptors, and the first real pressure of a destination.

What this means practically is that the useful intervention changes with the year. In the early years, tutoring that drills content is largely wasted; what helps is reading, writing stamina and the habit of finishing something. In the middle years, the highest-value work is teaching a student to recognise what a task is asking for, because criteria-based marking punishes a good answer to the wrong question more sharply than it punishes a weak answer to the right one. In the final years, time management and the personal project dominate, and content gaps become urgent only where they block a Diploma Programme choice.

Criteria, descriptors, the number of subject groups and the assessment arrangements are set by the International Baccalaureate and revised on its own cycle, so your school's MYP coordinator holds the position that applies to your child's cohort. A tutor who quotes a descriptor from memory should be asked where they read it. This matters more in MYP than almost anywhere else, because schools have genuine latitude in how they implement the programme, and two campuses can run the same year group quite differently.

The transition that worries parents most is the one at the end, into the Diploma Programme, and the worry is well founded but usually misdirected. The thing that does not transfer is not content; it is the shift from criteria that reward process and reflection to a system where a substantial part of the grade is decided by timed papers. sections.heading: The eight subject groups and criteria A to D
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme organises learning into eight subject groups: language and literature, language acquisition, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, arts, physical and health education, and design. Each is assessed against four criteria, each criterion carrying achievement levels rather than percentages, and the criteria differ by subject group even though they are labelled A to D in every one. This is the single most common source of parental confusion, and it is worth stating plainly: criterion B in mathematics and criterion B in sciences measure entirely different things, so a student who is weak at B in one is not necessarily weak at B in the other.

A few concrete examples of what the criteria actually reward. In mathematics, one criterion is about knowing procedures and another is about investigating patterns, which means a student can execute every method correctly and still score modestly because she has never been asked to generalise from a sequence of cases. In sciences, criteria cover inquiring and designing, and processing and evaluating, so a student who knows the science and writes a weak method or a generic evaluation loses marks that have nothing to do with knowledge. In language and literature, criteria separate analysing from organising and from producing text, which is why a student with strong ideas and poor structure lands in the middle.

This structure is what makes an MYP subject groups tutor in Santacruz West a different hire from a subject tutor. The question is never simply is she good at science. It is which criterion is low and what does that criterion reward. A good tutor's first move is to read the actual descriptors for the low criterion out loud with the student and translate each line into a question she can ask of her own work. Most students have never read them. Many have been told their level and never shown the sentence that produced it.

A limit worth stating because directory pages ignore it. No single person teaches eight subject groups well, and a listing offering MYP subject groups home classes Santacruz West wide is describing a panel rather than a teacher. Two related groups for one tutor is credible, mathematics with sciences or language and literature with individuals and societies. Beyond that, a home tutor for MYP subject groups Mumbai parents imagine hiring is a rota, and nobody in a rota has read your child's criterion breakdown.

sections.heading: Why are MYP marks out of 8 and not out of 100?
paragraphs: Because they are achievement levels against a criterion, not a proportion of a total. Each criterion has descriptors, and a level describes which descriptor the work matched: what the student did, not how much of a task she completed. That is why a level cannot be converted into a percentage and why dividing it by eight produces a meaningless number. It is also why the useful question to a teacher is never what percentage is this, but which descriptor did she match and what would the next one require. Schools in this area will answer that question if asked directly.

The local context matters here, and this is the part that genuinely distinguishes Santacruz West. Podar International School and Billabong High International School both run Santacruz campuses, and Ecole Mondiale World School sits across in Juhu. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with Podar International School, Billabong High International School, Ecole Mondiale World School or any school named here. The relevant fact is that because Podar International and Billabong High both have Santacruz campuses, the Cambridge Year 9 to Year 11 pipeline through this pocket is large and term dates are tightly shared, so the overwhelming majority of secondary-age children around an MYP family are on a percentage-and-rank system.

That creates a specific and avoidable harm. MYP parents here compare notes with neighbours whose children bring home seventy-eight per cent and a class position, conclude that their own child's six out of eight is a failure, and in some cases move a child out of the Middle Years Programme at Year 9 into a Cambridge cohort purely because the feedback feels more legible. Sometimes that move is right for other reasons. Made for this reason it is a decision taken on a measurement error, and it costs the student two years of continuity. If you are weighing it, ask the school to translate the criterion levels into what the student can and cannot yet do, and decide from that.

sections.heading: Does MYP home tuition in Santacruz West suit a Year 3 student?
paragraphs: For a student in the early or middle MYP years, an IB MYP tutor in Santacruz West who comes to the flat is not merely preferable, it is most of the point. What a thirteen-year-old needs is usually not explanation but supervised practice: writing a paragraph without being asked twice, finishing a task, reading something longer than a page, drawing the diagram rather than describing it. A tutor at the table can require all of that. A tutor on a screen can request it and will be nodded at. Most of the MYP home classes in Santacruz West we arrange for this age group run twice weekly and earlier in the evening than Diploma Programme sessions, which fits both the school day and a tutor's travel from Khar West or Vile Parle West.

Online becomes genuinely reasonable later, from the final MYP years onward, and for two specific purposes. Where a subject group has thin local supply, which in the Middle Years Programme means the arts, design and less common language acquisition options, a strong IB online tutor in Santacruz West is better than a local generalist who has never read the criteria. And for a Year 5 student doing personal project work, short online check-ins are an efficient way to keep momentum between school supervision meetings without consuming a full evening. Its weakness is constant: a screen cannot see a student who has stopped working.

Hybrid works well in the final MYP years and badly in the early ones. By Year 4 or 5 the division is natural: one home session for teaching, criteria work and accountability, one short online session for checking written work and keeping the project moving. Before that, splitting the arrangement dilutes the one thing you are actually buying, which is an adult in the room who will not accept a half-finished paragraph. We would not recommend hybrid for a Year 1 or Year 2 student however convenient it looks on a calendar.

A format to question. Group classes for MYP are offered widely and are hard to make work, because criteria-based assessment is individual by design: two students in the same class can have low levels in different criteria and need opposite interventions. If a group is offered, ask whether every student in it has the same low criterion in the same subject group, and how the tutor will know. A group assembled on year and subject alone is a school lesson repeated, and your child already attends that.

sections.heading: What should an IB MYP tutor in Mumbai be able to show you?
paragraphs: Four things, and the first one filters hard with any IB tutor Mumbai puts in front of you. Ask which MYP subject groups and which years they have taught, and for how long. Ask them to describe what one specific criterion in your child's subject group rewards, in their own words, without looking it up. Ask what they would do in the first session with a student whose levels are strong in one criterion and weak in another. And ask how you will both know at four weeks whether it is working. A tutor who cannot paraphrase a criterion has not taught the programme, whatever else they have done.

Our checks cover identity, qualifications and the specific claim to have taught these subject groups within the Middle Years Programme. Where a claim is unevidenced the profile says so rather than smoothing it in, which matters here because MYP teaching experience is the single most overstated line in the tutoring market. Diploma Programme experience is plentiful and MYP experience is genuinely scarcer, so a profile claiming both deserves a direct question about which one it actually has depth in.

What you can verify yourself is easier in MYP than in most programmes, because the criteria are published and your school will share them. After three sessions, ask your child which criterion she is working on and what the next descriptor would require. If she can answer, the tutoring is aimed at the right target. If she says we did chapter four, it is not. Look also at whether her written work is longer and more structured than a month ago, since in this programme the gap between knowing something and producing it is where most of the lost levels sit.

Two warnings. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed improvement in a level; criterion levels are judgements made by a teacher against descriptors on a particular piece of work, and nobody outside the school controls them. And be wary of a tutor who dismisses the criteria as bureaucracy and proposes to just teach the subject properly. That instinct is understandable and it is exactly how a student ends up well informed with the same report. An IB private tutor Santacruz West parents keep for several years is usually one who treats the descriptors as the actual syllabus.

sections.heading: The personal project in Year 5, and the line a tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The personal project in the final MYP year is a long piece of independent work with a school supervisor, a process journal and a product or outcome the student chooses. It is the first time most students are asked to manage something over months with no weekly deadline forcing progress, and that, rather than the subject matter, is what makes it hard. The marks reward the process as much as the product: how the goal was set, how the student planned, what she did when the plan failed, and how honestly she reflects. A beautiful outcome with a thin journal scores modestly, which surprises families every year.

The failure pattern is consistent and predictable. A capable student chooses an ambitious goal, does nothing for ten weeks because nothing is due, then produces the product in a fortnight and writes the journal retrospectively, inventing a process she did not follow. The product can be genuinely impressive. The report is weak, because a retrospective journal reads as retrospective to anybody who has marked a hundred of them, and because the criteria want evidence of decisions made at the time. The student concludes the project was unfair. It was not; it measured the thing it said it would measure.

What legitimate support looks like, and the boundary is sharper here than in any other MYP work. The school supervises the project and the student owns it entirely. A tutor's honest contribution is helping her set a goal that is specific enough to finish, insisting she write in the journal weekly whether or not anything happened, asking what she will do about the obstacle she has just hit, and reading her reflection to ask whether it is honest rather than flattering. A tutor who suggests content for the product, drafts the report or shapes the journal entries has crossed a line that carries academic honesty consequences far worse than a modest mark.

The timing argument is simple and it is the most useful thing on this page for a Year 5 family. Three or four tutoring sessions spread across the first half of the project, used to force weekly journalling and to narrow the goal, are worth more than fifteen sessions in the final month. They are also the cheapest intervention available, and they are the one piece of MYP work where parents reliably wait too long. If you are hiring an IB MYP tutor in Santacruz West for a Year 5 student, book the project support early and the subject support later, not the other way round.

sections.heading: What four weeks of MYP home tuition should change
paragraphs: Three things change in the first month of MYP home tuition anywhere in Mumbai, and none of them is a level. Your child should be able to name the criterion she is working on and say what the next descriptor would require, which you can test in one question at dinner. Her written work should be longer and visibly more structured, because in this programme the distance between knowing something and producing it is where most lost levels sit. And you should have had at least one message from the tutor you did not enjoy reading. A month of exclusively positive updates about a student whose report was mediocre means nothing has been diagnosed.

At one term, the school's own criterion levels in the specific criterion that was targeted, not the overall subject summary. This is where MYP progress is genuinely easier to read than examination-based progress, because the criterion is named and the descriptor is published: either the work now matches a higher descriptor or it does not, and the teacher can say which. Ask for that rather than for a general sense of improvement. If a full term has passed with no movement in the targeted criterion, the honest conversation is about whether the match, the diagnosis or the work between sessions is wrong.

At one programme stage, meaning the move into the Diploma Programme, be realistic about what tutoring is for. IB Gram does not guarantee grades or levels, no tutor on this platform may promise either, and a provider quoting success rates is selling rather than informing. What MYP tutoring reliably does is build criteria literacy, writing stamina and the habit of finishing, all three of which transfer. What it cannot do is make a fourteen-year-old care about a subject she has decided against, and a tutor who claims that power is overstating their role.

The limits are worth hearing plainly. Twice-weekly sessions will not fix a student who is not reading anything at all, and in the early MYP years reading volume predicts more than tutoring does. They will not substitute for the school's own feedback, which is the only source of the levels that actually appear on the report. And they will not resolve a situation where a student is in the wrong programme for her, which happens and which a good tutor will raise in month one rather than month ten.

sections.heading: How do you match an IB MYP tutor in Seven Bungalows to the right subject group?
paragraphs: By starting from the criterion, not the subject. A brief that says our Year 4 daughter is weak in sciences returns a science graduate. sections.heading: The eight MYP subject groups and five years in a Mumbai school
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme runs for five years, usually from around age eleven to sixteen, and organises everything into eight subject groups: Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design. Every student studies all eight, which is the first thing that surprises parents arriving from a national board where subject narrowing starts earlier. It is also why MYP students look busy without looking stressed until Year 4.

Two features sit across the eight groups rather than inside them. Interdisciplinary units ask students to use two subject groups on one problem, and they are marked on their own criteria, so a child can be solid in both parent subjects and still score poorly on the interdisciplinary task. Approaches to Learning are the skills the programme teaches explicitly: research, self-management, communication, thinking and social skills. When a report shows weakness across four subjects at once, the honest diagnosis is almost always self-management rather than four separate subject gaps.

Years 1 to 3 are broad and forgiving. Years 4 and 5 are where the programme tightens: subject content gets heavier, assessment tasks get longer, and in Year 5 the personal project arrives. Some schools in Mumbai also enter students for MYP eAssessment at the end of Year 5, and some do not, so ask your coordinator which route your school takes before assuming anything about external examinations.

This page stays inside the MYP. Diploma Programme subjects, Higher Level choices and the Extended Essay belong to other pages, and the Primary Years Programme to another again. sections.heading: Criteria A to D: what those letters on the report actually mean
paragraphs: Every MYP subject is assessed against four criteria labelled A, B, C and D, and the letters mean different things in different subject groups. In Mathematics they run roughly from knowing and understanding, through investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. In Sciences they cover knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. In Language and Literature they cover analysing, organising, producing text and using language. The letter alone tells you nothing until you know the subject group.

Each criterion is marked in bands against published descriptors, with task-specific clarifications written by the teacher. That has two consequences parents consistently miss. First, a band is not a percentage and cannot be converted into one, so a mid band is not a fail. Second, the four criteria are not all assessed on every task, which is why a child can have three marks in one subject and one in another and still be on track. Get the actual mark ranges and reporting conventions from your school, because they are set in the current subject guides and schools report them differently.

The pattern across hundreds of MYP reports is that criterion A, the knowledge criterion, is rarely the problem. Students in Mumbai schools are generally well drilled on content. The marks go on the skill criteria: designing a fair investigation, processing data and evaluating a method honestly, organising an extended piece of writing, communicating mathematical reasoning in words and diagrams rather than in a bare answer, and thinking critically about a source rather than summarising it.

That is the useful news, because skills are more teachable in four weeks than knowledge is. A student who has never been shown what an evaluation paragraph contains can be shown in one session and can practise it in three. A student who writes mathematics as a column of numbers with no sentences can learn to annotate a method in two. An MYP subject groups tutor in Seven Bungalows working criterion by criterion usually produces visible change in the work itself long before the next report arrives.

sections.heading: What the Mumbai MYP school year asks of a Year 4 or Year 5 student
paragraphs: Families in Seven Bungalows attend international schools across the western belt, and the nearest reference points are JBCN International School, Oshiwara and Billabong High International School. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with either of them or with any other school named here. The reason they appear is the calendar. MYP assessment is continuous rather than concentrated into an examination week, so the pressure points are task deadlines, and those vary by school in a way examination dates do not.

The shape of a Year 4 year is a steady accumulation of summative tasks across eight subject groups, with two or three landing in the same week several times a term. Nobody warns families about this because each individual task looks small. A student with weak self-management meets her first genuine crisis here, and it presents as a sudden drop in three subjects rather than as a single bad mark. A tutor who treats that as three content problems will waste a term.

Year 5 adds the personal project, and it is the most misunderstood piece of the programme. It is the student's own extended inquiry, supervised by a teacher at school, and it runs alongside everything else for months. The deadlines that hurt are not the final submission but the process ones: a proposal, a goal, evidence of the process kept as it happens rather than reconstructed later. A home tutor for MYP subject groups Mumbai parents engage in Year 5 usually earns their money on process discipline, not on the subject content.

Holidays interrupt differently in the MYP than in the DP. Because assessment is continuous, the Diwali week and the December break fall in the middle of task cycles rather than between them, and a project left untouched for three weeks loses its thread completely. Decide before the break whether sessions pause or move online, and for a Year 5 student keep at least one short check-in during a long holiday so the personal project does not go cold.

sections.heading: Are home classes better than online sessions for an MYP student in Mumbai?
paragraphs: For Years 1 to 3, home tuition is clearly better, and the reason is attention rather than pedagogy. An eleven or twelve-year-old alone in a room with a screen is one tab away from somewhere else, and the tutor cannot see it. A tutor at the table sees the moment attention goes and can change activity. Home classes also let a parent overhear the first two sessions without supervising them, which is how you find out whether the tutor actually explains or merely corrects.

By Years 4 and 5 the balance shifts, because the work changes. Essay feedback, personal project supervision and reviewing a science investigation design all work perfectly well on a screen with a shared document. An IB online tutor in Seven Bungalows is also the honest answer when the criterion you need help with is unusual: a Design technology tutor or a specific Language Acquisition pairing may simply not exist within a ten-minute drive of Versova, and a competent online specialist beats a nearby generalist every time.

An IB MYP home tutor in Seven Bungalows keeps one durable advantage at every year group. The most common cause of poor criterion marks in Years 1 to 3 is not understanding the task instruction, and an in-person tutor can read the actual task sheet off the school portal with the student sitting beside them, point at the command word, and watch the penny drop. Reading a task sheet together over a video call is possible and is noticeably slower.

Hybrid is where most families here settle. One in-person session a week after school for teaching and task decoding, plus a short online check-in to review a draft or confirm that a project step happened. For MYP specifically, the online half is often best used as accountability rather than teaching. Fifteen minutes on a Sunday evening confirming that the week's work exists prevents more lost marks than an extra hour of content.

Years 4 and 5: drafts, project supervision and design review work well online
Reading the school's own task sheet together is far faster in person

sections.heading: How to check an MYP tutor understands criterion-based marking
paragraphs: IB Gram verifies identity documents, qualifications against certificates, the subjects and levels a tutor says they have taught, and references where they exist. Unevidenced claims are removed rather than reworded. That is the baseline. For MYP there is one additional check that matters more than any credential, and it takes two minutes on the discovery call.

Ask the tutor to explain the difference between criterion A and criterion C in your child's subject group. Someone who has taught the programme answers immediately and in terms of what the student has to do. Someone who has only taught the content will talk about knowledge and application in general terms, or will ask you what the school means by it. That is not a disqualification for a Years 1 to 3 content gap, but it is disqualifying if the report says the skill criteria are where the marks are going.

Then ask two more things. How would you help with a personal project without doing any of it? The answer should be about questioning a goal, checking that the process journal is being kept as the work happens, and refusing to touch the product. And what will you show me at four weeks? For MYP the answer you want is a piece of your child's own work with the criterion descriptor beside it, so you can see the claim rather than take it.

The exit signals are unchanged. Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade or a band outcome, and of one who quotes results across other students instead of discussing your child's work. A tutor who wants a term paid up front before a single session is managing their own risk with your money. An IB private tutor Seven Bungalows families keep for several years is normally one who was comfortable being asked these questions and who told you something about your child in week one that the school had not.

A content-only tutor is fine for Years 1 to 3 gaps, wrong for skill criteria

sections.heading: What should we do about the jump from MYP Year 5 to the Diploma Programme?
paragraphs: Treat it as a change in how work is assessed, not a change in difficulty, and prepare for it in Year 5 rather than in the first DP term. The MYP marks four named skills against descriptors across continuous tasks. The DP marks a smaller number of high-stakes pieces, with examinations at the end and formal internal assessments along the way. A student who has been coasting on strong criterion A marks and weak skill criteria discovers in the first DP term that the skill criteria were the transferable part.

Three gaps account for most of the difficulty. The first is independent writing at length without a scaffold, because MYP tasks usually come with task-specific clarifications and DP questions do not. The second is quantitative fluency: MYP mathematics assesses communication and real-life application generously, and a student can score respectably while remaining slow at algebra, which then costs them in DP mathematics and in any science. The third is deadline management across a two-year horizon rather than a six-week task cycle.

The useful intervention in Year 5 is therefore unglamorous. Build algebraic fluency whether or not the report says mathematics is a problem. Practise writing one extended piece without a scaffold and without a criterion sheet. Use the personal project, which is the only two-term self-managed task in the whole programme, as deliberate training for DP deadline handling rather than as a box to be cleared. Parents comparing IB tuition fees in Seven Bungalows often find a single term of Year 5 work cheaper than a remedial first DP year, which is a real argument rather than a sales one.

One thing to resist. Do not use Year 5 to pre-teach DP content. Starting Higher Level material a year early sounds like preparation and usually produces a student who is bored in the first DP term and no better prepared, because the gap is in skills rather than in content coverage. And nobody can tell you in Year 5 what a student will score in Year 13. We do not guarantee grades and treat any prediction at this distance as marketing.
bullets: The DP changes how work is assessed, not only how hard it is
Writing at length with no scaffold is the first thing to practise
Build algebraic fluency in Year 5 even if mathematics looks fine
Use the personal project as training for two-year deadline management

sections.heading: What should change after four weeks of MYP tuition?
paragraphs: Changes in the work, not in the report, and they should be visible on a page you can hold. At four weeks of MYP home tuition expect a science write-up that contains a real evaluation naming a specific limitation rather than the phrase human error. Expect a mathematics solution with sentences in it explaining what was done and why. Expect an essay with a plan attached. Expect your child to be able to say which criterion a task is assessing before starting it. That last one is the single best predictor of a better band.

At one term expect the report to move, unevenly. The skill criteria respond first, because they are procedures. Criterion A often stays flat and occasionally dips, because a student who has stopped memorising and started reasoning is temporarily slower. Look at the trend across a full reporting cycle, and compare the same criterion in the same subject rather than comparing letters across subjects, which measures nothing.

Across a full MYP year, what good tutoring produces is a student who reads a task sheet properly, keeps a process journal as the work happens, hands in on time, and knows what an investigation needs before designing one. Those habits carry into the DP and into the personal project. They do not come with a number attached. IB Gram does not guarantee grades or bands, and the honest reason is that MYP marking is teacher-assessed against descriptors and depends on work we do not control.

It is also worth saying when not to hire an MYP tutor. If a Year 1 or Year 2 student is simply young and disorganised, a term of patient habit-building at home beats paid tuition. If the report is weak across six subjects, the first conversation should be with the school about workload and self-management, not with a tutor. And if a child is already doing four after-school activities, adding a fifth commitment is how you turn a dip into a refusal. Fewer, better-protected hours work better at this age than more of them.
bullets: Four weeks: a real evaluation, annotated mathematics, an essay plan
The best early sign is a child naming the criterion before starting a task
One term: skill criteria move first, criterion A can dip briefly

sections.heading: Starting MYP home classes in Seven Bungalows
paragraphs: Bring three things to the first session. The most recent report with the criterion letters as the school writes them. One marked piece of work, ideally one the child was disappointed by. And the task sheet for whatever is due next, because that is what the tutor and your child will work on together. With those, the first hour produces a diagnosis. Without them it produces a conversation you have already had with the school.

Expect session one to be mostly reading and talking rather than teaching. A good MYP tutor will read the task sheet aloud with your child, ask what the command word is asking for, ask what the criterion descriptor wants, and watch where the understanding breaks. Then they will do one short piece of work to see the habits: how the child starts, whether they plan, whether they check. Expect to be told one priority at the end, in a sentence.

On the slot, protect the early one. In Seven Bungalows a 4:30pm or 5pm weekday start is genuinely achievable because arrivals here are predictable, and for a student aged eleven to sixteen that is worth more than any other scheduling choice. Sixty minutes is usually right in Years 1 to 3 and ninety in Years 4 and 5. Our own listing label reads MYP subject groups IB Middle Years Programme (MYP), Years 1-5 tutor Mumbai, which is ugly but tells you exactly which five years a tutor is being matched for.

Then the rhythm: a written note every two to four weeks naming the criterion worked on, the evidence, and the next step. If the notes become reassurance, ask for the work. If the match is wrong, say so in week four rather than week fourteen, because there is no lock-in and an MYP year has enough task cycles left in it to recover. Parents searching IB tutors near me Seven Bungalows almost always find the shortlist easy and this last judgement hard.

Session one should decode a task sheet, not teach a topic
Protect a 4:30pm or 5pm start over anything after dinner

faqs.question: What do MYP tuition fees depend on in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Year group, subject group, scarcity and travel, and no page can honestly publish a rate. Years 4 and 5 cost more than Years 1 to 3 because the tasks are longer and the marking more demanding. Scarce subject groups such as Design or a less common Language Acquisition pairing cost more because few tutors teach them. Travel is priced in, so a tutor from Four Bungalows differs from one crossing the Western Express Highway. Ask for the per-session rate, whether marking a draft between sessions is included, and get it in writing first.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to Seven Bungalows straight after school in the evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the strongest practical reason to hire locally. Tutors based in Versova, Four Bungalows or Andheri West can make a 4:30pm or 5pm start because the roads here are short and parking is on the street, so there is no basement loop or visitor desk to absorb twenty minutes. For a student aged eleven to sixteen the early slot is worth more than the tutor's extra year of experience, because a tired child after dinner retains very little regardless of who is teaching.

faqs.question: Should a parent stay at home during an MYP session?
faqs.answer: Be in the flat, and for the first two sessions be within earshot without sitting in the room. You are listening for one thing: whether the tutor explains the task and the criterion, or simply corrects answers. Correcting answers looks productive and changes no band. After that, presence in the home is enough, and a parent in the room usually makes a thirteen-year-old perform rather than think. Set up a table with chairs on both sides, good light, no television in earshot, and the school portal accessible so task sheets can be opened.

faqs.question: What exactly do criteria A, B, C and D mean on my child's report?
faqs.answer: Four named skills per subject, marked in bands against published descriptors, and the letters mean different things in different subject groups. In Sciences they run through knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on impacts. In Language and Literature they cover analysing, organising, producing text and using language. A band is not a percentage and does not convert into one. Ask your school for the descriptors used in your child's subjects, because they come from the current MYP subject guides and schools report them in different formats.

faqs.question: How does a tutor help with the Year 5 personal project without doing it?
faqs.answer: By working on the goal, the process and the reflection, and never on the product. Useful help means stress-testing a goal that is too broad to finish, insisting the process journal is written as the work happens rather than reconstructed the week before submission, and asking the questions a supervisor asks so the student has already answered them. A tutor must not write, design, build or edit any part of the project, because it is formally assessed and the consequence of crossing that line falls on your child, not on the tutor.

faqs.question: My child's marks dropped in three subjects at once. Is that three problems?
faqs.answer: Almost never. A simultaneous drop across several subject groups in the MYP usually means self-management rather than content, because assessment is continuous and tasks cluster in the same weeks. The first thing to check is whether work is being handed in late or unfinished, not whether the content was understood. One tutor working on planning, task decoding and a weekly schedule often lifts all three subjects, where three subject tutors would each report that the content was fine. Raise it with the school as well, because they can see the submission record.

faqs.question: Is MYP easier than IGCSE or the CBSE curriculum?
faqs.answer: It is differently demanding, and comparing difficulty is the wrong question. The MYP spreads assessment across eight subject groups and marks named skills continuously, so it demands organisation and writing from an earlier age and less examination endurance. A content-heavy national board demands recall and examination technique sooner. Students moving in from either direction usually find the content manageable and the format disorienting for a term. The practical implication for tutoring is that a transferring student needs help with task formats and criteria first, and content second.

faqs.question: Do you cover students at JBCN International School, Oshiwara or Billabong High International School?
faqs.answer: We match tutors for students at schools across the western belt, and those two are simply the closest reference points to Seven Bungalows. IB Gram is an independent platform, not affiliated with either school or with any school named anywhere on this site. The school matters for scheduling rather than for content: because MYP assessment is continuous, its own task calendar decides which weeks are difficult, so a tutor should ask for the term's deadline schedule in the first conversation and build sessions around it.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an MYP student need?
faqs.answer: One a week for a single weak subject group, two if there is a task-management problem to fix as well, and rarely more than that in Mumbai where activity schedules are already full. MYP students are younger and already carry eight subject groups plus activities, so adding hours tends to produce resistance rather than marks. Two shorter sessions often beat one long one in Years 1 to 3 because attention spans are the binding constraint. In Year 5, one longer session plus a short project check-in is the arrangement that works best in our experience here.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover more than one MYP subject group?
faqs.answer: Frequently yes, and across Mumbai schools it is more reasonable in the MYP than at Diploma level, because much of the difficulty is criterion literacy rather than deep subject content. A tutor who understands how investigations are marked can usually help across Sciences and Mathematics; one who understands extended writing can help across Language and Literature and Individuals and Societies. Verify by asking which subject groups they have actually taught and for how long. An MYP subject groups home classes Seven Bungalows arrangement covering two groups also halves travel, which usually improves the rate.

faqs.question: What if we need to change tutor partway through the year?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we shortlist again. There is no lock-in and no notice period designed to hold you in place. Naming the problem specifically helps: criterion work never happens, no written reviews arrive, the tutor only checks homework, or your child dreads the slot. We match against that rather than sending a similar profile. Because MYP assessment is continuous, a change made in week four still leaves most of the task cycles in the year available, which is a genuine advantage over waiting until a report arrives.

faqs.question: Should we start MYP tuition in Year 3 to prepare for Years 4 and 5?
faqs.answer: Only if there is a real gap now. Hiring a tutor in Year 3 as insurance usually adds hours without adding skill, and it uses up a child's tolerance for extra work before the years that actually need it. What is worth doing in Year 3 at no cost is habit work: a weekly planner, handing in on time, and reading the criterion descriptor before starting a task. If those three are in place, Years 4 and 5 are far less likely to need outside help at all, which is the cheapest possible outcome.

sections.heading: Why does MYP feel easy until Year 4?
paragraphs: Because for three years the teacher is holding the scaffolding, and the marks reflect a joint effort nobody labels as joint. In MYP 1 to 3 a well-run classroom supplies the structure: the writing frame, the planning template, the reminder about what the criterion wants. A student who leans on all of it produces good work and a reassuring report. Then the scaffolding comes away by design, because independence is part of what the programme is built to develop, and the same student produces noticeably weaker work without having got worse at anything.

That is the conversation we have most often with parents in Sewri. Nothing happened in Year 4. What happened is that a dependency which was invisible became visible. Which is why the useful early work in MYP is so unglamorous: reading a task sheet aloud and saying what it actually asks for, planning before writing, checking a response against the criterion wording rather than against a feeling of having tried hard.

The second thing that changes around Year 4 is the kind of thinking being assessed. Earlier years reward knowing and applying. Later years weight analysis, evaluation and reflection much more heavily, and those are not harder versions of knowing. A student who has built a reliable method for reproducing content correctly has built the wrong engine for the second half of the programme, and rebuilding it takes a term of deliberately slower work.

Year 5 then stacks everything at once: the personal project runs alongside ordinary coursework, interdisciplinary units land in the same weeks as unit summatives, and anyone sitting optional external MYP assessment has a layer on top. Requirements and structures do get revised by the IB on its own cycle, so your school's MYP coordinator is the authority on what applies to your child's cohort. Ask them, not a tutoring page, and certainly not another parent in the car park.

sections.heading: Eight subject groups, four criteria, one common misreading
paragraphs: The eight MYP subject groups are Language and Literature, Language Acquisition, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics, Arts, Physical and Health Education, and Design. Each is marked against four criteria labelled A to D, and here is the misreading that costs families the most: the letters do not mean the same thing across groups. A report showing Criterion C weak in two subjects is not showing one weakness twice. In Mathematics, Criterion C concerns communicating mathematically. In Language and Literature it concerns producing text. A tutor hired to fix Criterion C in general is being hired to fix nothing in particular.

In practice the requests for an IB MYP subject groups tutor in Sewri arrive with recognisable signatures. A Year 2 Mathematics student whose answers are right and whose communication criterion is low is not bad at maths; the working is unreadable and the notation is improvised. A Year 4 Language and Literature student losing marks on the criterion about using the text is writing a strong opinion with no quotation anywhere near it. A Year 3 Sciences student whose inquiry criterion is low has written a hypothesis with nothing controlled in it.

Individuals and Societies punishes fluency without substance, because the criteria reward named sources and precise terminology over confident prose. Design is the group families most often underestimate: a polished final product with thin documentation of the inquiry and development stages scores modestly, which feels unfair to a student who worked hard on the artefact. Language Acquisition depends almost entirely on correct phase placement, and a student sitting a phase above their level spends the year quietly lost. Physical and Health Education surprises people by requiring written planning and reflection as well as performance.

What a good tutor does first is open the criterion wording next to the marked work and point at the phrase the work does not yet meet. Not explain the topic better. Not build confidence. Point at a phrase. If a candidate cannot do that for your child's group, they are teaching content and hoping marks follow, which works in some systems and does not work in this one. That is the screen we apply before a profile reaches you.

sections.heading: Does the Atal Setu widen the tutor pool for Sewri parents?
paragraphs: Yes, genuinely, and this is the one local fact worth building a decision around. Sewri is the island-city end of the Atal Setu, so Navi Mumbai tutors are a real option for families here for the first time, and the pool for IB home tuition in Sewri is no longer limited to people already living on the island. For common MYP requests that means more choice. For the scarce subject groups it occasionally means the difference between a specialist and nobody.

Understand why that matters by looking at the alternative. South Mumbai is dense and short-distance but slow: a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. Tutors here are usually matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs, which leaves families in Colaba or Walkeshwar choosing from whoever is already nearby. Being at a bridgehead is a structural advantage rather than a marketing line.

The ordinary geography still does most of the work. Sewri station sits on the Harbour Line from CSMT through Dockyard, the Sewri–Wadala corridor is the road a tutor actually drives, and an IB MYP home tutor in Sewri will normally also hold slots in Wadala, Mazgaon and Parel. Those four pockets are close enough that one tutor can run a sensible weekly circuit. Parel in particular has a deep supply of teaching talent, so Mathematics and Sciences requests are usually fillable within days.

Two cautions about the bridge, because enthusiasm for it outruns the facts. Node matters: a Vashi or Nerul based tutor can hold a 7pm Sewri slot through a term, while a Panvel based one will cancel by week five and nobody benefits from pretending otherwise. And the return leg is the problem, not the outward one, so we ask candidates what time they need to leave rather than what time they can arrive. Whatever building you are in, register the tutor once at the gate instead of raising a visitor pass weekly, and sort out parking before the first evening.

sections.heading: Report cards, portfolios and the Mumbai MYP year
paragraphs: Families from Sewri and the pockets beside it attend a small set of international schools, and JBCN International School, Parel and Bombay International School are the two that come up most in MYP conversations. Named as local context only: IB Gram is not affiliated with either school or with any school, and we do not guarantee grades. What their calendars do is decide when a criteria problem becomes visible to you, which is usually later than when it became real.

The Mumbai international year runs from roughly late March or April to the following March. MYP reporting is criterion-based, so a report card arrives with letters and descriptors rather than a single percentage, and that format conceals as much as it reveals. Two students with identical reported levels can be failing differently, one on planning and one on communication, and a parent reading levels alone cannot tell them apart. The teacher comment is where the real information sits, and it is the part most families skim.

Pressure points follow the calendar. The fortnight before the Diwali break in October or November compresses unit summatives because teachers want work completed rather than carried over, and that compression is what produces the October wave of enquiries. January and February then stack the personal project against ordinary coursework for Year 5, while Year 4 students are being warned that their current habits will not survive the step into the Diploma Programme. A tutor starting in January is triaging.

There is one more calendar feature worth using rather than fearing. Portfolio and process work accumulates across the year, which means evidence of improvement can be shown mid-year rather than waiting for a terminal mark. A student who starts MYP home classes in Sewri in June and keeps every planning sheet has a visible record by October that a tutor and a teacher can both read. Families who begin in a quiet month build that record. Families who begin in a panic have nothing to compare against.

sections.heading: Why MYP home classes beat a screen for a thirteen-year-old
paragraphs: The deciding factor is attention, not pedagogy. A thirteen-year-old alone with a laptop in a Mumbai flat at 7pm is one notification away from somewhere else, and MYP work requires sustained low-glamour effort of exactly the kind that evaporates under distraction. A tutor in the room is a social obligation. That sounds cynical and it is the single most reliable observation we have about this age band.

The second factor is process visibility. The things MYP marks, planning, investigating, communicating, reflecting, happen before the answer exists. A tutor sitting beside your child sees the plan not being made. A tutor on a screen receives the finished response and has to infer the process from the product, which is the hardest inference in teaching. Home tuition in Sewri is therefore our default for every MYP request, and the materials matter too: a design folder, a lab book, a marked-up novel, a task sheet with the criteria printed on the back.

Online is a real option for three situations and we arrange it without apology. The first is a scarce subject group, where the choice is a screen with the right specialist or a visit from a generalist. The second is a short review in the days before a summative, where forty focused minutes beat a cancelled hour. The third is the monsoon, when a 7pm arrival across the island is genuinely unpredictable and resentment builds on both sides. An IB online tutor in Sewri also suits a student who has a standing commitment that blocks the usual evening.

Hybrid is where most arrangements past one term land: one visit for the work needing supervision, one online session for review and questions. It is cheaper and more fragile. The online slot is the first casualty of a visiting cousin or a school production, and three lost slots in a term halve the arrangement without anyone deciding to halve it. If nobody at home will defend that slot, take two visits and pay for the travel rather than pretending the discipline exists.

sections.heading: Can a tutor prove they have marked MYP criteria?
paragraphs: Not with a certificate, which is why we ask them to talk instead. Our checks cover identity against government photo identification, the qualification claimed rather than asserted, and teaching history at MYP level specifically rather than at IB level. Then we ask a candidate to explain one criterion from your child's subject group in their own words and describe what distinguishes a mid-band response from a strong one. That conversation rejects more applicants than any document, because content knowledge is common and criteria literacy is not.

We also check the things that quietly end arrangements: the travel origin, whether the offered evening is free for a full term or only for this month, and whether the tutor will accept being registered once at a building gate rather than negotiating weekly with security. For families using the Atal Setu route we ask about the return journey specifically, because a tutor who can arrive comfortably and cannot get home by a reasonable hour will not last a term.

Your own checks are better than ours and take six minutes on the discovery call. Ask the candidate to read one marked piece of work and name the criterion phrase it does not yet meet. Ask what the first twenty minutes of session one contains, and listen for reading and asking rather than teaching. Ask what the four-week written review will say. Ask what they are not the right tutor for, because somebody claiming all eight subject groups across all five years is claiming eight different criteria frameworks.

One thing to settle explicitly before booking: what help with the personal project is and is not. A tutor may pressure-test the proposal, build checkpoints, keep the process journal honest and teach the structure of an evaluation. A tutor may not make the artefact or write the report. Ask the question directly on the call and listen for a clear line rather than a reassuring blur. Be wary of any tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, because none of this comes with one, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades.

sections.heading: Approaches to learning: the MYP skills Sewri parents never see marked
paragraphs: Running through all eight subject groups is a set of skills the programme calls approaches to learning, and they are the reason two students with the same understanding produce different work. Thinking, communication, social, self-management and research skills. They are taught across subjects rather than in one, they appear in criteria wording constantly, and because no report line is labelled with them, parents rarely realise this is what is actually being assessed when a criterion comes back low.

Self-management is the one that decides Year 5. A personal project is a self-managed task with a long horizon and no weekly deadline forcing progress, and a student with weak self-management does not produce a worse project; they produce a project compressed into the final fortnight, which then reads exactly like what it is. The fix is not motivational. It is a visible checkpoint structure the student designs themselves, reviewed weekly by somebody who does not accept vague progress reports. An IB MYP home tutor in Sewri doing this job well spends part of every Year 5 session on the plan rather than on the content.

Research skills are where the Mumbai-specific failure shows up. Students here are fluent searchers and poor evaluators. A Year 4 Individuals and Societies student can find fifteen sources in ten minutes and cannot say which two are worth citing or why, and the criteria reward precisely that judgement. Teaching it looks like slow work: take three sources on the same question, ask what each one would have to be wrong about for the others to be right. That exercise is worth more than another lesson on content.

Then there is the transition everyone worries about. MYP marks against criteria with descriptive bands; the Diploma Programme marks numerically with Higher Level and Standard Level choices, Internal Assessment deadlines, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge on top of six subjects. What carries across is not content. It is these skills: writing at length without collapsing, investigating without a handed-down method, judging sources, and managing a horizon longer than a week. A Year 5 student who leaves MYP with those is ready. One who leaves with good marks and none of them is about to have a difficult DP1.

sections.heading: How soon should MYP home tuition show in the work?
paragraphs: In four weeks, in the planning rather than in the marks. The checkable signals are specific: a first draft that now has a plan above it, a student who can state what the criterion asks for in their own words, and a task sheet that has been annotated rather than glanced at. All three are visible to a parent who does not understand the subject, which is the point of choosing them. If a month has passed and none of the three has appeared, call us in week five.

At one term, look for band movement in the single criterion you started with, and ignore the subject-level summary for now. MYP reporting aggregates, so a student who has moved from consistently low to consistently middling on investigation planning has made the exact progress you paid for and may show no change in the reported subject level for another cycle. We ask tutors to report criterion by criterion because subject averages hide the only thing worth watching.

At one full year, the honest measure is independence. Can your child start a piece of work before the tutor arrives. Can they produce a plan nobody asked for. Does the personal project have checkpoints they set themselves. A Year 4 student who reaches that point needs fewer sessions the following year, which is the outcome we aim at and the reason we sell no packages and hold no lock-in.

The limits deserve equal airtime. Two hours a week will not reverse three years of unread task sheets by December. No tutor fixes attendance, a phone on the table, or a student who has decided a subject is not theirs. Some matches fail on register rather than competence, and a fourteen-year-old who finds the tutor patronising will stop asking questions, after which the sessions are decorative. We replace without penalty, publish no success rates, and do not guarantee grades. Anybody in Mumbai promising a specific MYP level is inventing it. An IB MYP home tutor in Sewri is worth hiring for the planning habit, not for a predicted band.

paragraphs: Send four things in one message. The MYP year. The subject group, named as one of the eight. The criterion letter and its wording, copied from the report card.
