Tutors from the island city are offered as online matches instead, because a creek crossing twice a week in the evening peak does not survive a full term.

faqs.question: Does somebody need to be at home while the physics session runs?
faqs.answer: For the first session, yes, and within earshot for the first twenty minutes of it. You are checking whether your child is writing and talking more than the tutor is. After that most families in Ghansoli are in the flat without sitting in the room. The thing that genuinely needs a parent is the work between sessions: physics improvement comes from attempting problems alone and being wrong in private before being marked. A glance at the notebook twice a week does more for the outcome than supervising the taught hour.

faqs.question: My child knows the physics but writes answers that score badly. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually the command word and the register. IB Physics questions open with an instruction about how much reasoning to show, and a student who answers "state", "outline", "explain" and "deduce" in the same style is capped whatever they understand. "Show that" in particular needs the algebra written until the printed expression appears, and stopping one line short loses the mark. Units and symbols are the other half: an answer with no unit, or one where numbers went in before the algebra was finished, loses marks that were never about physics. Both are mechanical to fix within a few weeks of marked practice.

faqs.question: Should my child move from Higher Level to Standard Level Physics?
faqs.answer: Only after checking two things. First, the real entry requirement of the courses being considered, because many are satisfied by Standard Level and the assumption otherwise causes needless suffering. Second, whether the problem is the physics or the algebra underneath it, since a student whose algebra has never been taught properly is not yet a fair test of Higher Level. Ask your Diploma Programme coordinator what the internal deadline for a level change is, and get three weeks of marked work before the conversation. A decision made in a bad fortnight is usually regretted.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the scientific investigation without crossing a line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor can teach you how to test whether a research question is measurable, how to reason about uncertainty from the instrument and from the method, how to choose variables so the graph is a straight line, and how error bars constrain a conclusion. A tutor cannot choose your topic, write your analysis, supply data or edit the report into something that is no longer the student's own work. Any tutor who offers to do those things is a risk to the diploma rather than a help with it, and should be declined.

faqs.question: Which physics topics give Diploma Programme students the most trouble?
faqs.answer: Circular motion and gravitation, because the algebra compounds and the radius plays two different roles in the same question. Thermodynamics, where sign conventions get memorised and then misapplied. Electric and gravitational fields, where the analogy between them is useful until it misleads. Simple harmonic motion, where phase relationships are learned as pictures rather than as mathematics. And anything requiring logarithms, including decay and intensity. Higher Level stacks additional content on top of these, which is why the first HL term is where most students discover their algebra is the real obstacle.

faqs.question: How soon should we see progress in physics?
faqs.answer: It depends which problem the student has, and an honest tutor will tell you which at the start. A Middle Years Programme student whose gap is criterion language improves visibly in about four weeks. A Diploma Programme student rebuilding algebra may show nothing a parent can see at four weeks and be unrecognisable a term later; for that student the markers are symbols retained, units carried and a dimensional check attempted. Judge either case on an error log naming mistake types rather than on a run of percentages, and expect a harder paper to produce a lower mark sometimes.

faqs.question: What if the physics tutor turns out to be the wrong match?
faqs.answer: Say so at four weeks and a replacement is arranged with handover notes, so the next tutor starts from your child's error log rather than from scratch. Four weeks is the decision point because the markers for your child's particular problem either appeared or they did not. No lengthy justification is needed and nobody will argue the point. A tutor who did not suit your child frequently suits another family in Airoli or Vashi, and both can be true; mismatch in tutoring is far more often about working style than about competence.

faqs.answer: Often yes, for a student who can work alone. The scarcity is real along the Thane–Belapur Road: a tutor who has taken Diploma Programme Physics cohorts to an examination series and marked the papers is not on every street, and a strong online specialist beats a nearby generalist for a motivated DP2 student. sections.heading: How different is Diploma Programme physics from Middle Years Programme science?
paragraphs: Different enough that a strong Middle Years Programme (MYP) science student can arrive in Diploma Programme (DP) physics and drop a band inside a term. MYP sciences reward investigation design, reflection and clear communication across criteria, and a student who writes well is often carried by that. DP physics asks for the same investigation skills with far tighter numerical demands: algebra rearranged under pressure, units carried through every line, uncertainties propagated rather than mentioned, and answers written to the command term that was used. The content is not the shock. The precision is.

The Higher Level and Standard Level decision is the one families ask about most, and the honest answer depends on destination rather than ability. Higher Level (HL) physics adds depth on top of the shared core, which means more material and more time, and it is the sensible choice for a student aiming at engineering or physical sciences. Standard Level (SL) physics is a complete, respectable course and the right call for a student whose Higher Levels belong elsewhere. Make that decision with the current subject guide and your school's DP coordinator, not with a page on the internet, because the boards revise structure on their own cycles.

Primary Years Programme (PYP) and early MYP work does not need a physics specialist at all; it needs someone who keeps a child curious and numerate. The step that genuinely needs IB home tuition in Ghatkopar East is the one from MYP Year 5 into DP Year 1, usually taken in the first term of DP when the first topic test lands. Families who arrange a Physics tutor in Ghatkopar East for that specific transition, rather than waiting for the second-year panic, consistently have an easier time of it.

sections.heading: Which physics topics cost Ghatkopar East students the most marks?
paragraphs: Uncertainties and graph work, far ahead of anything else. On the data-analysis questions a student is expected to read a gradient with units, decide what the gradient physically represents, draw error bars that mean something and state an uncertainty without inventing precision. Students who understand the physics perfectly lose marks here because nobody ever made them practise it slowly. The second cluster is anything requiring a quantity to be linearised: turning a relationship into a straight-line form so a gradient can be extracted is a skill, and it is examined almost every session.

The third is command terms, and it is the quietest mark-loss on the paper. State, outline, describe, explain, deduce, determine, show that and sketch each ask for a different amount of work, and an answer that explains when it was asked to state wastes time while an answer that states when asked to explain loses the marks. On the extended-response paper, explain means a causal chain, and a student who writes two true sentences with no link between them scores one of three. A good tutor marks against the published scheme from the first fortnight so you can see this rather than hear about it.

Topic by topic, the reliable sore points are circular motion and the direction of the net force, simple harmonic motion and the phase relationships inside it, the field analogies between gravitation and electrostatics, thermodynamics where the sign conventions bite, and the Higher Level additional material that arrives late when energy is already low. A home tutor for Physics in Mumbai who starts with past-paper question types rather than reteaching chapters usually finds the gap in two sessions. Papers 1A, 1B, 2 and 3 appear on school timetables, and the current subject guide is where to check what each one covers for your child's session.

sections.heading: MYP sciences, Standard Level and Higher Level Physics: three different asks
paragraphs: In the Middle Years Programme (MYP), Physics usually arrives inside integrated sciences and is assessed against criteria rather than as a separate subject. The work rewards designing an investigation, processing data and evaluating a method, and students who are strong at content often score poorly because they have never been taught to write an evaluation that identifies a limitation rather than apologising for human error. An MYP student who learns to handle variables and uncertainty properly arrives in the Diploma Programme years ahead.

Standard Level Physics in the DP asks for the core concepts, quantitative problem solving and the scientific investigation. The jump that catches students is not the content volume; it is the expectation that a question will combine two areas without saying so. A question about a charged particle in a field is also a kinematics question, and a student drilled topic by topic will not see it.

Higher Level adds the additional higher level material on top of the same core, and it is a real step rather than an extension. The additional topics assume the core is automatic, so a student still thinking carefully about energy accounting will not cope with the HL extension of it. Choosing HL Physics on the strength of liking science, without checking mathematical fluency, is the most common expensive mistake we see in Mumbai households.

Confirm the current paper structure and the division between core and additional higher level material with your school's Diploma Programme coordinator. The International Baccalaureate revises subject guides on its own cycle, and the structure that applied to an older sibling may not be the one your child sits.

sections.heading: Why does a Physics student lose marks on a graph question?
paragraphs: Because a graph in Physics is a measurement instrument and students treat it as a picture. The marks sit in the gradient and the area, both of which carry units and physical meaning, and in understanding why the axes were chosen. A velocity-time graph's area is a displacement; a force-extension graph's area is energy stored; the gradient of a suitably linearised plot is often the quantity the question is actually asking for. A student who reads values off a curve instead of working with gradient and area will lose marks on every data-based question for two years.

The second place marks disappear is units and prefixes. Answers given in the wrong power of ten, millimetres used where metres were assumed, or a final figure quoted to five significant figures from data with two. The third is free-body diagrams, where the usual error is a missing force or an invented one, and where normal reaction on an incline gets drawn vertically. The fourth is sign conventions, which cause quiet havoc in energy and momentum questions where a direction has to be chosen and then kept.

The fifth is the command term. State, describe, explain, outline, discuss and justify ask for different things, and in Physics the gap between describe and explain is the gap between saying what happens and saying why it happens in terms of a named principle. A student who writes a correct description for an explain question has understood the physics and scored half. Physics home classes Ghatkopar West families book often spend an early session on nothing but rewriting answers to the command word.

Beneath all five sits the mathematics. Rearranging, standard form, trigonometry in resolving vectors, and the small amount of calculus that appears at Higher Level. A tutor who checks this first is not avoiding Physics; they are finding out whether Physics is the problem.

sections.heading: Can home classes replace a school Physics lab?
paragraphs: No, and any tutor who claims otherwise should be struck off your list. A school laboratory has apparatus, supervision and the data-logging equipment a scientific investigation needs, and none of that fits in a flat. What home tuition can do is everything around the practical: choosing a question that can actually be answered with the apparatus available, planning a range of values that produces a usable graph, processing data with proper uncertainty treatment, and writing an evaluation that identifies a real limitation of the method rather than blaming reaction time.

For the rest of Physics, home tuition is the stronger mode for most students, and for a specific reason. Physics problems are solved on paper with diagrams, and a tutor in the room can see whether the student drew one. The home classes we arrange across Mumbai for DP1 students are largely about building that process: read, draw, annotate, name the principle, then calculate. It is hard to enforce a process you cannot watch.

Online also handles investigation drafts well, because reading a draft and commenting on uncertainty treatment works the same on a screen. Hybrid is where most Physics arrangements end up: one home session for problem-solving process, one shorter online session for draft feedback or timed paper review, with the online slot moving to whenever the draft was finished.

sections.heading: How to tell a physicist from a Physics teacher
paragraphs: Ask them to explain why a question's data was plotted one way rather than another. A DP Physics teacher will talk about linearising a relationship so the gradient means something, and will mention what the intercept represents. An engineer who knows Physics will solve the question correctly and not see why the plotting choice is the question. Then ask what they do when a student's investigation has only five data points. The answer should be immediate and about range and repeats, not encouraging.

Our documented checks are narrow and we say so. Government photo identity, the degree being claimed, and evidence of teaching DP Physics at the level in question rather than tutoring science generally. Two references we can telephone. Base area and usual route on the profile. Where a tutor says they have supervised investigations and we have not been able to confirm it, the profile marks the claim unverified rather than letting it read as fact.

What you check is the first session's note. It should name the mechanism of failure, not the topic: does not draw free-body diagrams, reads values instead of gradients, loses prefixes, or writes descriptions for explain questions. A note from an IB physics home tutor in Ghatkopar West that says only needs to work on Physics is not a diagnosis. An IB private tutor Ghatkopar West families keep for two years is one whose first note was precise enough to disagree with.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: uncertainties are where the marks are
paragraphs: Most Physics investigations lose marks in the same three places, and none of them is the physics. The first is the research question: too broad to answer with school apparatus, or so narrow that the result is a single number with nothing to analyse. A question that produces a straight-line relationship across a decent range of values gives a student something to do; a question that produces three points and a shrug does not. Fixing this takes one session and it has to happen before any data is collected.

The second is uncertainty. Students record measurements without stating the instrument's resolution, propagate nothing, and then plot a graph with no error bars and draw a single best-fit line through it. The analysis marks live precisely there: an honest uncertainty estimate, error bars that reflect it, a maximum and minimum gradient, and a conclusion stated with an uncertainty attached. A student who learns this once uses it in every science subject afterwards.

The third is evaluation. The weakest evaluations list human error and suggest repeating the experiment more carefully. A strong evaluation identifies a specific limitation of the method, explains how it would have skewed the result in a known direction, and proposes a concrete methodological change. This is a writing skill with a scientific core, and it is teachable in two or three sessions, which is why it is such a good use of tutoring time.

What a tutor must not do is design the investigation or write any of it. A supervisor-style tutor generates candidate questions with the student, stress-tests the practicality, checks the uncertainty treatment after data collection, and comments on one draft. Anything more creates an academic honesty problem your child carries, not the tutor.

sections.heading: Higher or Standard Level Physics, and what actually differs?
paragraphs: Depth of reasoning rather than quantity of content, which is the part students discover too late. Both Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) Physics in the Diploma Programme (DP) cover the core of the subject, and the Higher Level course adds further material. The thing that separates them in the examination hall is not the extra topics but what a question expects you to do with any topic: Higher Level questions more often ask a student to combine two principles, to justify rather than state, and to carry algebra through several steps without a prompt. A student comfortable at Standard Level can meet exactly the same topic at Higher Level and not recognise the question.

This has a direct consequence for tutoring. A tutor who has taught Standard Level for years and is teaching Higher Level for the first time will cover the content correctly and set questions that are too kind. The marks appear fine in sessions and do not appear in tests. So level match is not a formality on this subject, it is the main thing, and it is worth asking a prospective tutor directly how a Higher Level question on a shared topic differs from a Standard Level one. A specialist will give you an example in one breath.

Below the Diploma Programme the subject exists differently. In the Middle Years Programme (MYP) physics sits inside integrated Sciences, assessed against criteria rather than percentages, and the predictive weakness is not content but the inquiry and processing criteria: designing a controlled investigation, processing data honestly, evaluating a method. In the Primary Years Programme (PYP) there is no physics, there is science inquiry, and a request for Physics coaching for a Grade 4 child is usually describing something else entirely, which an honest tutor will say on the call.

What we will not do is quote you paper configurations, durations or component weightings for any of these. The IB revises subject guides on its own cycle, so what applied to a cohort three years ago may not apply to yours. Name the papers and the skills, and get the structure from the current subject guide or your school's Diploma coordinator. A Physics tutor in Ghodbunder Road who quotes you a weighting from memory rather than from the document is telling you how carefully they read.

sections.heading: The Physics topics that cost the most marks
paragraphs: Ask any IB Physics home tutor in Ghodbunder Road, Mumbai and the first answer is units and prefixes, which is not a topic and is the largest single loss. Kilo, mega, micro, nano, centimetres entered as metres, grams left as grams in an equation that wanted kilograms. Students know all of this and lose marks on it under time pressure, and the only treatment is deliberate correction until writing the unit beside every quantity is automatic. A tutor who lets a numerical answer pass without a unit is building the habit that costs marks on every paper.

Then vectors and direction. Free-body diagrams drawn with forces missing or doubled, components resolved along the wrong axis, a negative sign dropped because the direction convention was never written down. This is where mechanics marks go, and it is a drawing discipline more than a conceptual one. After that, graph work: students read coordinates accurately and then lose marks because the gradient was calculated from two data points instead of a line of best fit, or because the gradient was reported without units and therefore without physical meaning.

Thermal physics and waves cost marks in the writing rather than the numbers, because the questions are often qualitative and students describe a phenomenon where they were asked to explain it. Electricity loses marks on circuit reasoning, particularly what happens to currents and potential differences when a component changes. At Higher Level, fields and induction are the point at which students who have been coping by pattern-matching stop coping, because the questions require a model to be applied rather than recalled.

Underneath all of it is the command term and the data booklet. "State", "describe", "explain", "deduce", "determine" and "outline" buy different amounts of writing, and an explanation written where a statement was wanted costs time without gaining marks. The data booklet is provided, and students who have not practised with it waste minutes hunting for a relationship they could have found in seconds. A home tutor for Physics Mumbai families find genuinely useful drills both. Physics home classes Ghodbunder Road parents keep for a full year are usually the ones where units, diagrams and command terms were fixed in the first month.

sections.heading: Uncertainty, graphs and the data booklet
paragraphs: Uncertainty is where Physics marks are won and lost in the practical work, and it is the part most students treat as paperwork. An instrument reading carries an uncertainty, that uncertainty travels through every calculation, and the final answer has a range rather than a value. Students who write a result to six decimal places from an instrument that resolves to the nearest millimetre have demonstrated the opposite of understanding, and markers notice. The habit to build is stating the uncertainty beside the measurement at the moment it is taken, not reconstructing it when the write-up is due.

Graphs are the second half of the same skill. Plot the data, draw a line of best fit, take the gradient from the line rather than from two data points, and attach units to the gradient so it means a physical quantity rather than a number. Error bars should be drawn where the uncertainty justifies them and should then be used, typically through steepest and shallowest acceptable lines, to give the gradient its own uncertainty. A student who draws error bars and never refers to them again has done the work and not collected the marks.

Linearisation is the technique that makes most of this tractable and is rarely taught explicitly. Many physical relationships are not straight lines, so you rearrange the relationship until plotting one quantity against another gives a straight line whose gradient is the thing you want. A student who can do this will design a better investigation, because they will plan which quantities to measure in order to get a straight-line graph, rather than measuring whatever is convenient and hoping the analysis works out. Three sessions on this in Diploma Year 1 pays back across both years.

The data booklet deserves its own practice. It is provided in the examination and students who have not used it regularly waste minutes searching, or worse, use a relationship without checking what its symbols stand for in that context. Working through past papers with the booklet open, until finding a relationship takes seconds, is unglamorous and worth real marks. A Physics IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai families book for Diploma Year 1 should be building all four of these habits before content revision begins. Confirm the current practical and assessment requirements with your school's coordinator rather than relying on any online summary, including the material behind this page.

Partial credit appearing where there used to be nothing, because method is visible. Graph questions answered with a gradient that has units. For a student losing marks on discipline rather than understanding, one grade of movement across a term is a reasonable expectation. For a student whose mathematics is genuinely weak, the first term goes on the mathematics and the Physics grade follows later, and a tutor who promises otherwise in September is managing you.

At one examination cycle, the limits are worth stating plainly. Tutoring narrows the gap between what a student understands and what they can demonstrate under timed conditions, and it builds habits that compound across two years. It does not replace classroom teaching or laboratory time, it cannot fix a scientific investigation whose data was collected badly in a fortnight the school allocated, and it does nothing for a student who does no problems between sessions. faqs.question: My child understands Physics but keeps getting the numbers wrong. Is that a Physics problem?
faqs.answer: Usually not. It is most often a mathematics problem inside a physics question: rearranging an equation, handling prefixes and unit conversions, or resolving a vector into components. faqs.question: How should we handle uncertainty in the scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Record it beside each measurement as it is taken, rather than reconstructing it when the write-up is due. Instrument resolution sets the uncertainty, that uncertainty travels through the calculations, and the final result is a range rather than a single number. Then use it: error bars drawn where justified, and the gradient's own uncertainty found from the steepest and shallowest acceptable lines. Students who draw error bars and never mention them again have done the work without collecting the marks. Confirm current practical requirements with your school's Diploma coordinator.

sections.heading: Standard Level, Higher Level and the extra topics: which physics course is your child on?
paragraphs: Confirm the level in writing before you hire, because the additional Higher Level material is the part most tutors have least experience of. At Standard Level the subject rewards a student who can reason carefully about mechanics, energy, waves, fields, electricity, thermal behaviour and nuclear physics, and who can write that reasoning down. Higher Level adds depth that requires genuine mathematical comfort as well: electromagnetic induction with its direction conventions, capacitor behaviour over time, and the quantum and nuclear material that students either find fascinating or find impossible.

The level decision should follow a university requirement rather than ambition. Physics at Higher Level is demanding in a way that is not obvious from the Standard Level experience, and it falls in the same months as every other deadline in the Diploma Programme (DP). A student taking it because it looks serious rather than because a course demands it will pay for that in their other subjects. If you are unsure, ask what your child wants to study and whether that course actually asks for Higher Level physics, because many do not.

Paper structure is the part you should not take from any page, including this one. Physics examinations have included a multiple-choice component, a data-based component and an extended-response component, commonly referred to as Papers 1A, 1B and 2, and the IB revises its subject guides on its own cycle so the arrangement differs between cohorts. Ask your Diploma Programme coordinator which papers your child's cohort sits, what each one contains and what the current investigation requirements are, then hand the answers to the tutor in week one.

For students below the Diploma Programme the useful work is different and mostly invisible. Comfort with rearranging equations before substituting numbers, reading a graph as a relationship rather than as a picture, and the habit of drawing a situation before attempting it are what decide whether Higher Level physics is available later. A Physics tutor in Girgaon working with a younger student should spend more time on those three things than on content, because the content arrives soon enough and the habits do not.

sections.heading: Where do physics marks actually go on Papers 1A, 1B and 2?
paragraphs: In the extended-response work, marks go to distinct physics statements and nothing else. An explain question wants a mechanism and a consequence: what changes, why it changes, and what follows. Students lose marks by giving the consequence without the mechanism, or by restating the question with the word because inserted. A deduce question wants the reasoning visible, not the conclusion. A describe question wants no reasoning at all, and students who supply it waste time they needed elsewhere. Teaching the difference between these command terms is dull and it is worth more marks per hour than any topic.

In the data-based work, the losses are technical and highly teachable. Plotting with error bars and then drawing a single line through them with no comment on the range of possible gradients. Treating a line of best fit as if it were the only line. Giving a gradient to five significant figures from a hand-drawn graph. Mishandling the propagation of uncertainty through a multiplication or a power. Failing to state whether an intercept is physically meaningful. None of this requires more physics knowledge; it requires a method, applied every time.

The content topics that produce predictable mistakes are worth listing, because a tutor who names them in the first conversation is telling you something. Free-body diagrams drawn without every force, or with invented ones. Centripetal force treated as an additional force rather than as a resultant. Energy questions answered without stating which system is being considered. Path difference and phase difference used interchangeably. The sign of gravitational or electric potential. Internal resistance ignored in a circuit question that depends on it. Specific heat capacity and latent heat swapped. Mass defect and binding energy per nucleon confused.

The scientific investigation sits apart from all of this and carries real weight. Its common failures are not about physics at all: a research question too broad to answer with the equipment available, a method that varies two things at once, raw data recorded without uncertainties, processing shown without explanation, and an evaluation that lists improvements rather than assessing what the results actually support. A tutor can help legitimately with every one of those, provided the investigation itself remains the student's own work.

sections.heading: Why do strong mathematicians lose physics marks on graphs?
paragraphs: Because a graph in physics is an argument, and mathematics trains students to treat it as an object. A mathematically able student plots accurately, draws a confident line and reports a gradient to several figures, having done everything correctly except the thinking the question wanted. The physics question wanted to know what the gradient means, whether the intercept is physically possible, what the spread of the data permits them to claim, and whether the relationship they assumed is actually supported. None of that is mathematics, and none of it is taught by doing more mathematics.

The method that fixes it is mechanical and can be taught in a few sessions, then practised for a term. Plot with error bars drawn, not implied. Draw the steepest and shallowest lines the error bars allow as well as the best fit, and take the gradient uncertainty from the difference between them rather than from a feeling. Report the gradient to a number of significant figures the data can support, which is usually two or three rather than five. Say what the gradient represents in physical terms, with units. Then state whether the intercept means anything or whether the model simply fails near zero.

Uncertainty propagation is the other half and students get it wrong in a predictable order. Absolute and fractional uncertainty confused. Fractional uncertainties added when quantities are multiplied, which is right, and then also added when they are added, which is not. A power applied to a quantity without multiplying its fractional uncertainty by that power. A final answer quoted with an uncertainty to three significant figures, which is physically meaningless. Each of these is a rule, and rules are the easiest thing in the subject to teach once somebody notices they are missing.

This is also the part of physics that works best at a Girgaon dining table, which is worth saying because the absence of a laboratory makes families assume home tuition is limited. Graph paper, a sharp pencil, a ruler, a calculator and somebody watching is the entire requirement. Physics home classes Girgaon families book for a DP1 student are at their most valuable here, because the skills transfer straight into the investigation and into every data-based paper the student will sit afterwards. An IB physics home tutor in Girgaon who opens with this rather than with content has read the situation correctly.

faqs.question: His maths is strong but his physics answers lose marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Because physics pays for distinct statements and he is probably making one and repeating it. An explain question wants a mechanism and a consequence: what changes, why, and what follows from it. A mathematically confident student often jumps to the result, which is correct and collects a fraction of the marks. The fix is mechanical rather than conceptual. He is taught to plan an answer as a numbered list of separate physics points before writing prose, and to check that no two points say the same thing. Most students see the difference in marks within a month, with no change in their understanding.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the scientific investigation if there is no lab at home?
faqs.answer: Yes, because most of the assessed difficulty is not in the apparatus. A tutor can question whether the research question is answerable with the school's equipment, which is the single most valuable intervention and has to happen early. They can insist that only one variable changes, that raw data is recorded with uncertainties, that processing is explained rather than displayed, and that the evaluation assesses what the results support rather than listing improvements. The data collection happens at school. The work has to be your child's own, and a tutor who offers to supply the method is a risk rather than a help.

faqs.question: What is the difference between describe, explain and deduce in a physics answer?
faqs.answer: Describe asks what happens with no reasoning, so adding reasoning wastes time you need elsewhere. Explain asks for the mechanism and its consequence, which means at least two distinct statements and usually three. Deduce asks you to show the reasoning that leads to a conclusion, so the conclusion alone earns little. Students lose predictable marks by answering one with another, and the loss is spread thinly across a whole paper, which makes it invisible in a report. It is among the cheapest things to teach and among the first things a competent tutor will drill.

faqs.question: How do we practise uncertainties and error bars at home?
faqs.answer: With graph paper, a pencil, a ruler and somebody checking, which is why this part of physics suits home tuition particularly well. The routine is fixed: plot with error bars drawn rather than implied, add the steepest and shallowest lines the bars permit, take the gradient uncertainty from the gap between them, report significant figures the data can support, then say what the gradient means physically. For propagation, learn the rules properly: fractional uncertainties add when quantities multiply, and a power multiplies the fractional uncertainty. Practise on somebody else's messy data rather than on perfect textbook tables.

faqs.question: Should she take physics at Higher Level if she wants medicine?
faqs.answer: Check what the specific courses she is interested in actually require, because many do not ask for Higher Level physics and some do not ask for physics at all. Taking it unnecessarily costs time she will want for chemistry and biology, and the additional Higher Level material is genuinely demanding rather than simply longer. Ask the Diploma Programme coordinator to help you read the entry requirements for a realistic list of universities before deciding. A tutor can tell you whether she could cope with Higher Level; only the course requirements can tell you whether she should.

faqs.answer: Scarcity above everything else. The pool of people who have genuinely taught the additional Higher Level material and supervised investigations is much smaller than the pool who can teach Standard Level content, and that sets the rate more than any other factor. Session length and frequency change the hourly figure, and twice-weekly bookings often carry a lower rate because travel is spread across two lessons. faqs.question: He says he understands it in class and cannot start the question at home.
faqs.answer: That is the fourth failure mode and it is about habit rather than knowledge. In class the context is given: the topic is on the board, so the method is obvious. Alone with an unfamiliar question, he has no routine for working out what the question is about. The treatment is a fixed opening sequence drilled until it is automatic: draw the situation, label what is known and what is wanted, decide which physical principle applies, rearrange, then substitute. It takes a few weeks of being made to do it in that order even when he thinks he can see the answer.

faqs.question: How much of physics teaching needs equipment we do not have?
faqs.answer: Less than most parents assume. The written components reward reasoning, derivation, graph interpretation and uncertainty handling, all of which need paper rather than apparatus. Where equipment genuinely matters is in building physical intuition, and a good tutor substitutes for that with everyday demonstrations, careful diagrams and video of real experiments rather than pretending it is unnecessary. The school supplies the laboratory and should be left to. If a tutor tells you your child needs home equipment to make progress in Diploma Programme physics, treat that as a reason to ask more questions.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting physics tuition in DP2?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a different plan and honest expectations. In DP2 the job is triage rather than teaching: identifying which topics carry the most recoverable marks for this student, drilling command terms and data handling because those pay across every paper, and rescuing whatever can be rescued in the investigation. That is real value. What it is not is the same arrangement as starting in DP1, where the same tutor would be preventing the problems rather than mitigating them. A tutor who offers you the same outcome in either case is not being straight with you.

faqs.question: He loses marks on free-body diagrams. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Quickly, and it tends to improve several topics at once. The errors are nearly always the same three: a force left out, a force invented because it feels like it should be there, and centripetal force drawn as an additional arrow rather than understood as a resultant. The fix is a checklist applied every time until it stops being needed: what touches the object, what acts at a distance, nothing else. Mechanics marks improve first, then circular motion, then anything involving equilibrium. It is among the best returns on a few sessions in the whole subject.

sections.heading: Higher Level or Standard Level physics: what actually differs?
paragraphs: Higher Level (HL) physics is not Standard Level (SL) with more hours. It adds topic areas the Standard Level student never meets, including rigid body rotational mechanics, aspects of relativity, and a deeper treatment of quantum and nuclear physics. It also changes the style of question: Higher Level problems routinely require a student to recognise which two principles apply and in which order, with no hint in the wording. A student who is comfortable answering single-principle questions and uncomfortable deciding between principles is the classic Higher Level casualty, and the diagnosis is visible by about week four.

Both levels share the same spine, and that spine is where most of the marks sit: mechanics and energy, thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism, and fields. The Diploma Programme now presents these through a framework that groups ideas rather than listing isolated topics, and the paper structure has been revised within recent cycles, so confirm with your child's coordinator which papers they will sit and what each one contains rather than relying on any webpage, this one included. What does not change is that one paper tests short recall and data analysis while another tests extended reasoning.

The level decision, where it is still open, belongs with the coordinator and should rest on what your child intends to study afterwards. Several engineering pathways expect Higher Level physics; several design, architecture and life science pathways do not. A tutor's useful contribution is evidence rather than advice: after four weeks and two timed papers they should be able to say whether the Higher Level course is survivable with support. A profile reading Physics IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 tutor Mumbai says nothing about Higher Level experience, so ask which level they taught last term and how many investigations they have supervised.

sections.heading: Where do IB physics marks disappear?
paragraphs: Uncertainties first, and by a wide margin. Absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty get confused; uncertainties are quoted to too many figures; the uncertainty in a gradient is guessed rather than found from maximum and minimum lines through the error bars. Data-based questions carry marks that a student who understands the physics perfectly will still fail to collect, because nobody taught the arithmetic of error. This is the fastest available improvement in the subject and schools rarely have time for it, which makes it the obvious first job for home tuition.

Graph linearisation is second. A student is given a relationship that is not a straight line and asked to plot something that is, then to extract a physical quantity from the gradient. The failures are mechanical: plotting the wrong variable, forgetting that the gradient now carries combined units, or reading the intercept without asking what it physically means. Third is free-body diagrams, where the recurring error is drawing centripetal force as an extra arrow alongside the real forces, or drawing forces on the wrong body entirely. Fourth is the chain-of-reasoning answer, where each causal link earns a mark and students supply only the conclusion.

Then there is a short list of reliable topic confusions worth naming, because a tutor who knows them saves weeks: terminal potential difference against electromotive force once internal resistance is involved, path difference against phase difference in interference, specific heat capacity against latent heat in a cooling curve, and the three inverse-square fields treated as three unrelated topics rather than one idea with three constants. Physics home classes Goregaon East families book usually spend the first month on uncertainty and graphs and the second on this list, in that order, because the first raises marks across every paper.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: a measurable question beats an interesting one
paragraphs: The investigation is an independent piece of experimental work and the most common cause of lost marks is the research question, decided in an afternoon and never tested for feasibility. The question needs one clearly identified independent variable the student can actually change, a dependent variable they can actually measure with the apparatus their school has, a sensible range, enough repeats to say something about uncertainty, and a reason for the whole thing rooted in physics rather than curiosity. A question about an interesting phenomenon that cannot be varied is not a research question. It is a topic.

A good tutor treats topic selection as an elimination exercise across two or three sessions. The student brings five ideas. Four are killed out loud, with reasons stated: no measurable variable, apparatus not available, range too narrow to show a trend, physics above or below the course level. The fifth gets refined into a question with a predicted relationship, which matters because a prediction is what makes the analysis possible. Only then does the student book laboratory time. Doing it the other way round, collecting data and then deciding what the question was, produces the drafts that cannot be rescued in March.

A draft returned with fewer structural comments and more physics comments is real progress even when the predicted mark has not moved. Ask your tutor to put the two drafts side by side rather than describe the improvement, and if the earlier draft cannot be produced, nothing was being tracked.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on physics questions they clearly understood?
faqs.answer: Because Diploma Programme physics pays for reasoning, not conclusions. Extended-response questions are marked as a chain of causal links, and a student who writes the correct final statement without the steps collects credit for one link out of several. faqs.question: What are uncertainties and why do they matter so much?

Students confuse absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty, quote uncertainties to too many significant figures, and guess the uncertainty in a gradient instead of taking it from maximum and minimum lines through the error bars. Schools rarely have time to drill this properly, which is why it is the first job for a physics tutor and the fastest visible improvement available. It also decides a large part of the scientific investigation mark.

Data comes from your school's apparatus on your school's timetable, and no tutor should attempt to replace that. What home classes cover is everything around the experiment: designing a question with a measurable variable, deciding range and repeats, setting up the uncertainty treatment before the apparatus is touched, then the analysis and the writing. faqs.question: Is my child's problem physics or mathematics?

If the algebra fails, the fix is mathematics and a physics tutor will spend half of every session on it anyway. If the translation fails, that is physics and specifically the habit of identifying which principle applies. Many students have both, in which case fix the algebra first because everything else depends on it.

sections.heading: From MYP sciences to Diploma Programme physics
paragraphs: In the Middle Years Programme (MYP), physics is taught inside integrated sciences and assessed against criteria that reward investigation design, data processing and reflection alongside knowledge. A student can score well there with modest algebra and strong writing. That is not a flaw in the programme; it is what the programme is for. It does mean the report card from Year 5 of the MYP is a weak predictor of Diploma Programme (DP) physics performance, and this surprises families every single year.

The Diploma Programme course changes the demand sharply. Content density rises, questions become multi-step, and the mathematics stops being incidental. Students are expected to rearrange equations under time pressure, read gradients and intercepts off unfamiliar graphs, handle units and orders of magnitude without hesitating, and reason from a diagram they have drawn themselves. Higher Level (HL) adds further topics and depth on top of the Standard Level (SL) core, which is a separate conversation covered on our Higher Level page rather than here.

There is a third transition worth naming because nobody warns parents about it: the shift from being taught physics to being assessed on physics thinking. Early in the DP, questions still look like the ones in the textbook. By the second year they look like nothing the student has seen, and the skill being tested is applying familiar principles to an unfamiliar situation. Students who revise by memorising worked examples hit a wall here, and it feels to them like a sudden collapse rather than a predictable one.

For physics across IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 a tutor in Mumbai covers a wide span of demand, and matching level matters more in this subject than in most. A capable MYP science teacher is not automatically ready for DP physics, and a DP specialist is often impatient with a Year 8 student who needs confidence and number sense. An IB home tutor in Goregaon West should be matched to one of those jobs, not asked to cover both because one family has two children.

sections.heading: Which physics topics lose the most marks?
paragraphs: Kinematics graphs come first, and they keep costing marks for years. Students confuse the gradient of a displacement graph with the gradient of a velocity graph, read area when they should read slope, and describe motion in words that do not match the line in front of them. Next are forces, where the real failure is the free-body diagram. A student who draws forces acting on two bodies in one picture, or who invents a centrifugal force, has lost the question before any arithmetic happens.

Then the clusters that reliably appear in enquiries from this corridor. Circular motion and gravitation, where direction of acceleration is counter-intuitive. Electric circuits, where students can apply formulas but cannot reason about what happens when a resistor is added in parallel. Thermal physics, where specific heat capacity and latent heat questions are mechanical but the energy bookkeeping is not. Waves and superposition, where phase is the obstacle. And fields, where the distinction between potential and field strength is permanently slippery.

The command words are a separate tax. State wants a bare answer. Describe wants what happens. Explain wants a causal chain with physics in it. Deduce wants a conclusion justified from given information. Determine expects a numerical result with working. Sketch and draw have different accuracy expectations. Students who answer every one of these as though it said describe can know the physics thoroughly and still sit in the middle bands, and this is among the fastest things an IB physics home tutor in Goregaon West can fix.

Finally the practical side. Every Diploma Programme science student produces an individual scientific investigation, and it is marked against criteria rather than for ambition. The common failures are a research question too broad to answer, uncertainty treated as decoration rather than analysis, and a conclusion that does not engage with the data actually collected. A tutor's proper role here is to question the student's design and check their reasoning, never to write any part of it. For current paper structure, assessment components and investigation requirements, use your school's Diploma coordinator and the live subject guide, since the International Baccalaureate revises these on its own cycle.

sections.heading: Why are physics marks usually lost in the mathematics?
paragraphs: Because physics assumes mathematics that the mathematics course has not yet made automatic. A Diploma Programme physics question may require rearranging a formula with the unknown in a denominator, substituting values in standard form, taking a ratio to eliminate a constant, reading a gradient from axes that are not labelled in the obvious units, and then quoting an answer to a sensible number of significant figures. Every one of those is a mathematics skill, and a student who is merely competent rather than fluent spends all their working memory there and none on the physics.

This is why we so often shortlist a physics tutor who is comfortable teaching the underlying algebra directly rather than working around it. The first month of a well-run physics engagement frequently looks like mathematics: rearrangement drills with physical quantities, unit analysis as a routine check, standard form arithmetic without a calculator, and reading five unfamiliar graphs a week purely to practise extracting gradient and intercept. Parents sometimes query this. It is the fastest available route to physics marks, and it is why IB physics home tuition in Goregaon West often begins with a month that looks nothing like physics.

Units and significant figures deserve their own paragraph because they are pure free marks. A correct numerical answer with the wrong unit, or quoted to eight decimal places because that is what the calculator said, loses credit that cost nothing to keep. Uncertainty is the same story in the practical work: students treat it as a box to fill rather than as analysis that should affect the conclusion. Three sessions on unit discipline and uncertainty handling, early, pay back across the entire remaining course.

The last mathematical weakness is proportional reasoning, and it is the deepest. Asked what happens to the force if the separation doubles, a fluent student answers instantly from the structure of the relationship; a weaker one reaches for numbers. Most of the harder multiple-choice items are built on exactly this ability. A home tutor for Physics in Mumbai who drills proportional reasoning as a habit is doing something no amount of topic revision replaces, and it is one of the few interventions that visibly changes performance on unfamiliar questions.

sections.heading: Higher Level or Standard Level physics: what actually differs?
paragraphs: The additional content is the visible difference and the smaller one. Higher Level physics extends several themes a Standard Level student meets only in outline, and those extensions tend to be the mathematically heavier parts of the course, where reasoning has to be sustained across several steps rather than applied once. The less visible difference, and the one that costs more marks, is the expected depth of explanation. A Higher Level question will ask why a quantity behaves as it does and expect a chain of physical reasoning, where the Standard Level version of the same topic accepts a correct relationship stated and applied.

The written components are where that expectation lands, and the structure has been revised recently enough that you should confirm the current arrangement with your child's Diploma Programme coordinator rather than trusting an older description. Broadly, one component tests recall and quick application across the breadth of the course, another tests the handling of experimental data, and another tests extended structured reasoning on fewer, longer questions. Those are three different skills. A student can be comfortable with two of them and lose a grade on the third, which is why IB physics home tuition in Govandi should be organised around components rather than around chapters.

Before the Diploma Programme the picture is different. A Middle Years Programme (MYP) student meeting physics inside the sciences subject group is marked against published criteria, so the scientific inquiry and communication criteria matter as much as the content. Families booking IB home tuition in Govandi for a Year 4 or Year 5 student usually need help with investigation design and written reflection, not with examination technique. Say which programme your child is in, because a Higher Level specialist is often the wrong person for criterion-marked middle-years work.

sections.heading: Which parts of IB physics lose the most marks?
paragraphs: The word explain, more than any topic. A very large share of lost marks in physics goes to answers that describe what happens when the question asked why it happens. A student writes that the current decreases when the resistance increases, which is a description, where the mark needed the relationship named and applied to the specific circuit. Teaching the difference between state, describe, explain, deduce and justify is unglamorous work that moves grades, and most students have never had it taught explicitly. A physics tutor who reads your child's answers against a mark scheme rather than an answer key will find this pattern in the first fortnight.

Second is the diagram. Students who do not draw a free-body diagram get vector problems wrong at a rate that has nothing to do with their understanding of forces, because the signs and components were never fixed on paper. The same applies to ray diagrams, field patterns and circuit redraws. Making the diagram compulsory before any calculation is a habit, not a concept, and it is one of the fastest interventions available. Physics home classes Govandi parents book in the first Diploma Programme year often spend the early sessions on precisely this.

Third is data and uncertainty, which is where strong mathematicians are often weakest. Reading a gradient and saying what it physically represents, choosing what to plot so a relationship becomes linear, propagating uncertainties sensibly, deciding how many significant figures an answer is entitled to, and commenting on whether a result is consistent within its error bars. These are examinable skills in their own right, and they are also exactly what the internal investigation is assessed on. A student who treats uncertainty as a box to tick loses marks twice, once in the written component and once in their own coursework.

sections.heading: Can physics home tuition work in Govandi without a lab?
paragraphs: Yes, because the part of physics a tutor is needed for is not the part that requires apparatus. The practical work belongs to the school, which has the equipment, the technicians and the supervision requirements, and no home tutor should be replicating it. What a tutor does with experimental physics at your dining table is the reasoning around it: designing a workable research question, choosing variables that can actually be controlled, deciding what to plot, propagating uncertainties, and writing an evaluation that identifies real limitations rather than reciting human error. IB physics home tuition in Govandi is at its most valuable in exactly this territory.

For the rest of the subject, in-person sessions win for the same reason they do in maths: the tutor needs to watch the work being produced. A student who will not draw a free-body diagram unprompted needs somebody present to stop them calculating, and that intervention is immediate across a table and awkward on a screen. Simple apparatus a tutor can bring or improvise still has a place, a pendulum on a string or a ball rolling down a book, not to generate data but to make a relationship physical for a student who has only ever met it as an equation.

Online physics is genuinely strong for some of the work, and honest about it is better than dismissive. Marking a past paper, walking through a mark scheme, reviewing an investigation draft and running timed question practice all transfer well, and an IB online tutor in Govandi can reach a Higher Level specialist who lives nowhere near the Eastern Suburbs. Where online struggles is the first-year student who needs supervision to build habits. Most families here end up hybrid by the second term: one session at home for teaching, one online for marking and draft feedback, which also keeps the travel sustainable enough that your slot survives February.

sections.heading: The scientific investigation: where a tutor helps and where they must not
paragraphs: The individual scientific investigation is the piece of physics coursework that worries families most, and it is also where tutoring is most often done wrongly. The student designs and carries out their own investigation and writes it up, and the assessment rewards the quality of the thinking rather than the sophistication of the apparatus. Ask the Diploma Programme coordinator for the current requirements and the school's internal deadlines, and plan backwards from those dates rather than from anything written online, because the guidance is revised on the organisation's own cycle.

Where a tutor legitimately earns their fee is before a word is written. The most common failure is a research question that cannot be answered with the equipment available or that has no real independent variable to vary. The second is scope: a student who sets out to investigate something genuinely interesting and ends up with four data points and no uncertainty analysis. The third is the evaluation, where weak write-ups list generic limitations instead of identifying what specifically constrained this particular set of measurements. Talking through those three things across two sessions in September saves a crisis in January.

Where a tutor must stop is the writing and the data. Reading a draft and saying the uncertainty treatment is thin, or that the graph choice hides the relationship, is feedback. Supplying the paragraph, restructuring the analysis or suggesting what the numbers should have been is not, and schools are required to check authenticity. The honest position is that a physics tutor can make a student's own investigation markedly better by asking harder questions earlier, and cannot responsibly do more than that. A tutor who offers more is offering your child a risk.

sections.heading: Standard Level or Higher Level physics: what actually changes?
paragraphs: Higher Level physics adds topics that are examined in their own right, extends the mathematical demand across most of the course, and assumes a level of independence that a strong Year 11 student does not automatically possess. The additional content is not an appendix; it changes how the earlier material is questioned, so a Higher Level student meeting fields, induction or quantum topics is also being asked harder questions about mechanics than her Standard Level classmates. Confirm exactly what each level contains against the current subject guide your school works from, because the IB revises these on its own cycle.

The mathematical step is the one that catches Mumbai students out. Higher Level physics expects comfort with algebraic rearrangement under pressure, with logarithms and exponentials in decay and discharge contexts, and with reading gradients and areas off graphs as physical quantities rather than as numbers. A student taking physics at Higher Level alongside Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation rather than Analysis and Approaches can find the mathematics arriving faster than her other course is supplying it, and that is worth checking in the first term of DP1.

The combination question matters as much as the level. Three experimental sciences at Higher Level means three scientific investigations in the same part of the year, and in practice all three suffer. Physics alongside Chemistry at Higher Level is a common and manageable pairing; physics alongside two other Higher Level sciences and an Extended Essay in a fourth subject is a plan that works on paper and not in January.

If the level looks wrong, raise it with the Diploma Programme coordinator early, because the window to drop from Higher Level to Standard Level narrows as the course progresses and schools handle it differently. A Physics tutor in Grant Road can give you evidence for the conversation in two or three sessions: set Higher Level questions and watch whether the difficulty is the physics, the mathematics or the independence. Those three have different answers and only one of them means the level is wrong.

sections.heading: Which physics topics do Grant Road students lose marks on?
paragraphs: Mechanics first, and not for the reason parents assume. Students can recite the relationships and still lose marks because they do not draw a free-body diagram, so forces get double-counted, a normal reaction is given the wrong magnitude, or a component is resolved along the wrong axis. The fix is mechanical in both senses: insist on a labelled diagram before any algebra, every time, until it becomes automatic. It looks like a trivial discipline and it recovers marks across the whole paper.

Then the topics where the physics is counter-intuitive rather than hard. Circular motion, where students apply a centrifugal force that does not exist in the frame they are working in. Electromagnetic induction, where the direction of the induced effect is the whole question and the magnitude is the easy part. Thermal physics, where specific and latent heat questions fail on bookkeeping rather than on principle. And anything involving fields, where the sign conventions for work done and potential catch out students who have learned the formulae without the model.

The waves and oscillations group separates the upper grades. Simple harmonic motion is manageable as algebra and hard as a phase relationship, so students lose marks on questions asking when, not how much. Interference and diffraction questions fail on path difference reasoning. At Higher Level the quantum and nuclear topics reward students who can describe a model in words, which is exactly the skill that students strong in mathematics tend not to have practised.

The largest single pile of lost marks, though, is in the writing. sections.heading: Uncertainties, graphs and the marks nobody teaches you to claim
paragraphs: There is a block of marks in Diploma Programme physics that sits outside the topics and that most students never learn to collect. It concerns measurement: how an uncertainty in a reading propagates through a calculation, what a sensible number of significant figures is for a derived quantity, what an error bar on a plotted point means, and what the gradient of a line through those points can and cannot be claimed to show. It appears in the data-based component and again in the investigation, and it is marked the same way in both.

Linearisation is the skill that recovers most of it. Students are taught relationships and then shown data that does not form a straight line, and the move of rearranging the relationship so that a straight-line graph becomes possible is the single most valuable technique in the course. A student who can decide what to plot against what, and can then say what the gradient and intercept physically represent, is collecting marks that her classmates leave on the table. This can be taught in about four sessions and is almost never taught in a hurry at school.

The uncertainty side is more mechanical and equally neglected. Absolute and fractional uncertainty, how they combine through products and powers, and how to express a final result so that the precision claimed is honest. Students lose marks by quoting a value to six figures when the measurement supports two, which reads to an examiner as not understanding what was measured. The habit takes a few weeks to install and then persists.

Where this becomes urgent is the investigation. A student from Tardeo or Girgaon with good data and no uncertainty analysis has produced a school project rather than a piece of physics, and the evaluation section is where that becomes visible. Physics home tuition that spends three sessions on measurement before the investigation is written changes the ceiling of the whole component. Check the current subject guide and your school's documentation for how the component is assessed, because the detail is revised and no summary should be trusted for it.

sections.heading: Papers 1A, 1B and 2: where Mumbai physics students lose marks
paragraphs: Six areas take most of the marks, and only one of them is a knowledge gap. Free-body diagrams come first: students draw forces that are not acting, omit the normal force on a slope, or treat a Newton third-law pair as acting on the same body. Second, circular motion, where the direction of acceleration is counter-intuitive and a sentence about centrifugal force costs the mark. Third, the distinction between field and potential in gravitation and electrostatics, including the sign conventions that make negative potential energy confusing.

Fourth is uncertainty and data handling, which is its own discipline. Reading a graph gradient, drawing error bars, deciding significant figures, propagating an uncertainty through a calculation, and linearising a relationship so it can be plotted as a straight line. Students who have never practised this lose marks in the data-analysis section regardless of how well they know the content. Fifth is the energy and thermal work, where specific heat capacity and latent heat plateaus on a heating graph get confused year after year.

Sixth, and the largest, is the explain question answered as a description. A student who writes what happens rather than why it happens scores almost nothing on a question worth several marks. The structure that works is mechanical: name the principle, state the relationship, then connect it to the specific situation in the question. The IB physics home classes in Hiranandani Estate, Thane we arrange spend real time on this, because it is the cheapest set of marks available to most students.

Command terms are the other half of the same problem. State needs one line. Outline needs the key points without development. Explain needs causal reasoning. Deduce requires a conclusion drawn from given information. Compare and contrast requires both similarities and differences. Sketch and draw are not interchangeable. A student who learns these six properly gains marks across every paper without learning any new physics.

sections.heading: What should a physics tutor diagnose in the first hour?
paragraphs: Whether the problem is physics, mathematics, or language, and a competent tutor separates those three inside an hour using three tasks. First, ask the student to draw a free-body diagram for a block on a slope and talk through it out loud. Students who draw a force that is not acting, or who cannot say what exerts each force, have a conceptual gap. Students who draw it correctly and then cannot resolve the components have a mathematics gap. The diagram sorts them in four minutes.

Second, hand over a velocity-time graph and ask what is happening and how they know. This is the single most revealing task in physics, because interpreting a gradient and an area is the skill the whole data-analysis section rests on. A student who says the object is going faster when the line slopes up, but cannot say what the area underneath represents, has a specific and fixable hole. Third, give an explain question and ask them to say the answer aloud before writing it, which exposes whether they can reason causally or only describe.

The written diagnosis that comes out of that hour should name the category, not just the topics. Conceptual gaps need re-teaching from physical situations. Mathematical gaps need drilling on rearrangement, indices and trigonometry, often alongside their maths course. Language gaps need the explain structure and the command terms, which is the quickest improvement available in this subject. A tutor who proposes starting at theme A and working forwards has produced a timetable rather than a diagnosis.

faqs.question: My child knows the theory but fails the exam. What is actually wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually command-term technique, not knowledge. The most common pattern is a student who answers an explain question by describing what happens rather than why, which scores almost nothing on a multi-mark question. The remedy is structural: name the physics principle, state the relationship, then connect it to the specific situation in the question. The second most common cause is mathematics, where a student understands the physics and cannot rearrange the equation fast enough. A good tutor separates those two in the first hour rather than guessing for a month.

faqs.question: How much help can a tutor give with the scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Enough to make it a strong piece of the student's own work, and no more. A tutor can legitimately discuss possible research questions, help think through variables and uncertainties, explain what the assessment criteria are asking for, and give feedback on a draft the student has written. A tutor who provides the experiment, processes the data or writes the report is handing your child academic misconduct, which schools are well equipped to identify. Ask any tutor where they draw this line, and treat a vague answer as the answer itself.

faqs.question: Is Higher Level physics manageable alongside Higher Level maths?
faqs.answer: It is a demanding combination that suits some students very well and overloads others. The risk is workload concentration: both subjects carry an internally assessed piece, and the drafting periods can overlap. faqs.question: Why do students lose so many marks on uncertainties?
faqs.answer: Because it is a separate discipline that most students never practise deliberately. Reading a gradient, drawing error bars, deciding significant figures, propagating an uncertainty through a calculation and linearising a relationship so it plots as a straight line are procedural skills, not content knowledge. They appear in the data-analysis part of the examination and in the investigation, so the same gap costs marks twice. Thirty minutes a fortnight on this for a term usually produces a visible gain, and it is often the easiest improvement available in the whole course.
